title.zh: 卷一百一十五 載記第十五 苻丕 苻登
title.en: Volume 115 Records 15: Fu Pi; Fu Deng
title.raw: 卷一百一十五 載記第十五 苻丕 苻登 Volume 115 Records 15: Fu Pi; Fu Deng

sentences.zh: 苻丕 苻登

translations.literal: Fu Pi; Fu Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi; Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 苻丕，字永叔，堅之長庶子也。

translations.literal: Fu Pi, courtesy name Yongshu, was the eldest son of Fu Jian born to a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi, whose courtesy name was Yongshu, was Fu Jian’s eldest son by a concubine.

sentences.zh: 少而聰彗好學，博綜經史。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and loved learning; he broadly combined the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was bright and bookish, with a wide command of the classical corpus and historical records.

sentences.zh: 堅與言將略，嘉之，命鄧羌教以兵法。

translations.literal: Jian spoke with him about generalship and strategy, praised him, and ordered Deng Qiang to teach him military methods.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian discussed campaigns and strategy with him, was impressed, and had Deng Qiang instruct him in the art of war.

sentences.zh: 文武才幹亞於苻融，為將善收士卒情，出鎮於鄴，東夏安之。

translations.literal: In civil and military talent and capacity he was second to Fu Rong; as a general he was good at winning the feelings of soldiers and officers; when he went out to garrison Ye, the eastern Xia was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: His gifts in civil and military affairs stood just below Fu Rong’s; as a commander he knew how to win his men’s loyalty, and when he was posted to Ye the eastern heartland stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 堅敗歸長安，丕為慕容垂所逼，自鄴奔枋頭。

translations.literal: When Jian was defeated and returned to Chang'an, Pi was pressed by Murong Chui and fled from Ye to Biantou.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian’s defeat and retreat to Chang’an, Fu Pi was driven from Ye by Murong Chui and fled to Biantou.

sentences.zh: 堅之死也，丕復入鄴城，將收兵趙、魏，西赴長安。

translations.literal: At Jian's death, Pi again entered Ye city, intending to gather troops in Zhao and Wei and go west to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian died, Fu Pi re-entered Ye, planning to raise forces in Zhao and Wei and march west toward Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 會幽州刺史王永、平州刺史苻沖頻為垂將平規等所敗，乃遣昌黎太守宋敞焚燒和龍、薊城宮室，率眾三萬進屯壺關，遣使招丕。

translations.literal: It happened that the Inspector of You, Wang Yong, and the Inspector of Ping, Fu Chong, had repeatedly been defeated by Chui's generals Ping Gui and the like; thereupon (Wang Yong) sent the Administrator of Changli, Song Chang, to burn the palace buildings at Helong and Ji, led thirty thousand troops forward to encamp at Huguan, and dispatched envoys to summon Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Youzhou governor Wang Yong and Pingzhou governor Fu Chong had suffered repeated defeats at the hands of Murong Chui’s generals such as Ping Gui, so Yong sent Changli prefect Song Chang to torch the palaces at Helong and Ji, moved thirty thousand men up to Huguan, and sent envoys urging Fu Pi to join him.

sentences.zh: 丕乃去鄴，率男女六萬餘口進如潞川。

translations.literal: Thereupon Pi left Ye, leading more than sixty thousand persons of both sexes forward to the Lu River region.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi then quit Ye, shepherding well over sixty thousand civilians and soldiers toward the Lu River basin.

sentences.zh: 驃騎張蠔、并州刺史王騰迎之，入據晉陽，始知堅死問，舉哀于晉陽，三軍縞素。

translations.literal: The General of Agile Cavalry Zhang Hao and the Inspector of Bing, Wang Teng, welcomed him; they entered and occupied Jinyang, and only then learned the report of Jian's death; they observed mourning at Jinyang, and the three armies wore white.
translations.idiomatic: General of Agile Cavalry Zhang Hao and Bingzhou inspector Wang Teng received him; once they had taken Jinyang they learned for certain that Fu Jian was dead, and the army mourned there in full white.

sentences.zh: 王永留苻沖守壺關，率騎一萬會丕，勸稱尊號，丕從之，乃乙太元十年僭即皇帝位於晉陽南。

translations.literal: Wang Yong left Fu Chong to defend Huguan, led ten thousand cavalry to join Pi, urged him to assume the exalted title; Pi followed this, and in the tenth year of Taiyuan arrogated the emperor's position south of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong left Fu Chong to hold Huguan, rode in with ten thousand horse to meet Fu Pi, and pressed him to take the throne; Fu Pi agreed, and in the tenth year of Taiyuan (385) he unlawfully declared himself emperor south of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 立堅行廟，太赦境內，改元曰太安。

translations.literal: He established Jian's traveling shrine, greatly pardoned within the territory, and changed the era name to Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a mobile shrine to Fu Jian, proclaimed a general amnesty within his domain, and adopted the era name Tai’an.

sentences.zh: 置百官，以張蠔為侍中、司空，封上黨郡公；

translations.literal: He established the hundred officials, appointing Zhang Hao Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, enfeoffing him Duke of Shangdang commandery;
translations.idiomatic: He installed his bureaucracy, naming Zhang Hao Palace Attendant and Minister of Works with the ducal title of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 王永為使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、車騎大將軍、尚書令，進封清河公；

translations.literal: Wang Yong as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, advanced enfeoffment to Duke of Qinghe;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong received the staff of authority, the palace post, supreme military command, the chariots-and-cavalry generalship, and the chief ministership, and was promoted to Duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 王騰為散騎常侍、中軍大將軍、司隸校尉、陽平郡公；

translations.literal: Wang Teng as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Central Army, Colonel Director of Retainers, Duke of Yangping commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Teng was made cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, general of the central army, colonel director of retainers, and Duke of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 苻沖為左光祿大夫、尚書左僕射、西平王；

translations.literal: Fu Chong as Grand Master of the Left, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Xiping;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chong became grand master of the left, senior vice minister of the secretariat, and Prince of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 俱石子為衛將軍、濮陽公；

translations.literal: Ju Shizi as General of the Guard, Duke of Puyang;
translations.idiomatic: Ju Shizi was appointed general of the guard and Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 楊輔為尚書右僕射、濟陽公；

translations.literal: Yang Fu as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Jiyang;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu was named right vice director of the secretariat and Duke of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 王亮為護軍將軍、彭城公；

translations.literal: Wang Liang as General Who Protects the Army, Duke of Pengcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang became general who guards the army and Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 強益耳、梁暢為侍中，徐義為吏部尚書，並封縣公。

translations.literal: Qiang Yier and Liang Chang as Palace Attendants, Xu Yi as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, all enfeoffed as Dukes of counties.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Yier and Liang Chang were made palace attendants, Xu Yi minister of personnel, and each was ennobled as a county-level duke.

sentences.zh: 自余封授各有差。

translations.literal: As for the rest, enfeoffments and appointments each had their gradations.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining appointments and noble ranks were distributed according to merit and station.

sentences.zh: 是時安西呂光自西域還師，至於宜禾，堅涼州刺史梁熙謀閉境距之。

translations.literal: At this time the General Who Pacifies the West Lü Guang returned his army from the Western Regions and reached Yihe; Jian's Inspector of Liang, Liang Xi, plotted to close the borders and resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile General Who Pacifies the West Lü Guang was marching home from the Western Regions and reached Yihe, where Fu Jian’s Liangzhou governor Liang Xi planned to shut the frontier and block him.

sentences.zh: 高昌太守楊翰言於熙曰：「「呂光新定西國，兵強氣銳，其鋒不可當也。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Gaochang, Yang Han, spoke to Xi, saying: "Lü Guang has newly pacified the western states; his soldiers are strong and his qi sharp; his edge cannot be withstood."
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang prefect Yang Han warned Liang Xi: “Lü Guang has just subdued the west; his troops are strong and their morale keen—no one should meet that spearhead head-on.”

sentences.zh: 度其事意，必有異圖。

translations.literal: Measuring the matter's intention, he is sure to have a different design.
translations.idiomatic: Judging his intentions, he must be nursing ambitions of his own.

sentences.zh: 且今關中擾亂，京師存亡未知，自河已西迄於流沙，地方萬里，帶甲十萬，鼎峙之勢實在今日。

translations.literal: Moreover now Guanzhong is disturbed and chaotic; the capital's survival or destruction is not known; from west of the River down to the flowing sands, the territory is ten thousand li, with one hundred thousand armored men; the tripod-standing posture is truly in this day.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Guanzhong is in turmoil and the fate of the capital uncertain; west of the Yellow River all the way to the desert lies a realm ten thousand li across and a hundred thousand soldiers under arms—the moment for a three-way standoff is now.

sentences.zh: 若光出流沙，其勢難測。

translations.literal: If Guang exits the flowing sands, his situation will be hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lü Guang emerges from the desert, his next move will be impossible to predict.

sentences.zh: 高梧穀口，水險之要，宜先守之而奪其水。

translations.literal: Gaowu valley mouth is a choke point of water danger; it is fitting first to guard it and seize their water.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaowu defile is a waterless choke point; you should seize it first and cut off their supply of water.

sentences.zh: 彼既窮渴，自然投戈。

translations.literal: When they are exhausted and thirsty, naturally they will cast aside their spears.
translations.idiomatic: Left parched and desperate, they will throw down their weapons of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 如其以遠不守，伊吾之關亦可距也。

translations.literal: If because it is distant he does not guard it, the pass of Yiwu can also be used to resist.
translations.idiomatic: If he will not hold a distant position, the Yiwu pass can still serve as a barrier.

sentences.zh: 若度此二要，雖有子房之策，難為計矣。

translations.literal: If he passes these two crucial points, even with Zifang's stratagems, it will be hard to plan.
translations.idiomatic: If he slips past both choke points, even a strategist like Zhang Liang could not salvage the situation.

sentences.zh: 地有所必爭，真此機也。

translations.literal: There are grounds that must be contested; truly this is the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Some ground simply must be fought for, and this is that moment.

sentences.zh: 」熙弗從。

translations.literal: " Xi did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liang Xi refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 美水令犍為張統說熙曰：「主上傾國南討，覆敗而還。

translations.literal: The Magistrate of Meishui, Zhang Tong of Qianwei, persuaded Xi, saying: "The lord above tilted the whole state south on campaign, was overturned and defeated, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tong of Qianwei, magistrate of Meishui, urged Liang Xi: “Our sovereign staked the realm on a southern expedition and came home in ruinous defeat.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂擅兵河北，泓、沖寇逼京師，丁零雜虜，跋扈關、洛，州郡奸豪，所在風扇，王綱弛絕，人懷利己。

translations.literal: Murong Chui monopolizes troops north of the River; Hong and Chong raid and press the capital; Dingling miscellaneous barbarians run rampant in Guan and Luo; prefecture and commandery treacherous heroes, wherever located, fan like wind; the royal net is slack and severed; each person harbors benefit to self.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui holds Hebei at sword point, Fu Hong and Fu Chong press the capital, Dingling and other tribes swagger through the Guanzhong and Luoyang heartland, local strongmen rise wherever the wind blows, imperial authority has collapsed, and every man is out for himself.

sentences.zh: 今呂光回師，將軍何以抗也？

translations.literal: Now Lü Guang returns the army; with what will the General resist?
translations.idiomatic: Now Lü Guang is marching back—how do you propose to stop him?”

sentences.zh: 」熙曰：「誠深憂之，未知計之所出。

translations.literal: " Xi said: "Truly I deeply worry about it; I do not know where a plan may come from.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liang Xi replied, “I share that fear, but I see no clear course.”

sentences.zh: 」統曰：「光雄果勇毅，明略絕人，今以蕩西域之威，擁歸師之銳，鋒若猛火之盛于原，弗可敵也。

translations.literal: " Tong said: "Guang is heroic, resolute, brave, and firm; his clear strategy surpasses others; now with the awe of having swept the Western Regions and grasping the sharpness of a returning army, his edge is like fierce fire blazing on the plain; it cannot be opposed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhang Tong said, “Lü Guang is bold, resolute, and abler than ordinary men. Fresh from conquering the west and leading a seasoned army home, his attack will spread like wildfire across dry grass—no force can stand against it.

sentences.zh: 將軍世受殊恩，忠誠夙著，立勳王室，宜在於今。

translations.literal: The General's family for generations has received extraordinary favor; loyalty and sincerity have long been manifest; establishing merit for the royal house is fitting in this present.
translations.idiomatic: Your house has long enjoyed the dynasty’s favor and a reputation for loyalty—now is the time to earn your place in its service.

sentences.zh: 行唐公洛，上之從弟，勇冠一時。

translations.literal: The Duke of Xingtang, Luo, is the Sovereign's younger male cousin; his bravery crowns the age.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Xingtang Fu Luo, the emperor’s cousin, is the bravest man of the hour.

sentences.zh: 為將軍計者，莫若奉為盟主，以攝眾望，推忠義以總率群豪，則光無異心也。

translations.literal: For the General's planning, nothing is better than honoring him as covenant lord to gather the multitude's hope, promoting loyalty and righteousness to command the host of heroes; then Guang will have no different heart.
translations.idiomatic: My counsel is to acknowledge him as leader of the league, win the gentry’s trust, and rally the magnates under the banner of loyalty—then Lü Guang will have no cause to turn on you.

sentences.zh: 資其精銳，東兼毛興，連王統、楊璧，集四州之眾，掃凶逆于諸夏，甯帝室於關中，此桓文之舉也。

translations.literal: Relying on his crack troops, east annex Mao Xing, connect Wang Tong and Yang Bi, gather the multitudes of four provinces, sweep the fierce rebels in the various Xia, pacify the imperial house in Guanzhong—this is a deed of Huan and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Use his elite soldiers, join forces eastward with Mao Xing, link up with Wang Tong and Yang Bi, concentrate the four provinces’ hosts, drive the traitors from the Central Plain, and restore the court in Guanzhong—an achievement worthy of Duke Huan or Duke Wen of Jin.”

sentences.zh: 」熙又不從。

translations.literal: " Xi again did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: ” Again Liang Xi would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 殺洛於西海，以子胤為鷹揚將軍，率眾五萬距光於酒泉。

translations.literal: He killed Luo at Xihai, appointed his son Yin General Who Spreads Might, led fifty thousand multitudes to resist Guang at Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Fu Luo at Xihai, named his son Yin general who spreads might, and sent fifty thousand men to oppose Lü Guang at Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 敦煌太守姚靜、晉昌太守李純以郡降光。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Dunhuang, Yao Jing, and the Administrator of Jinchang, Li Chun, with their commanderies surrendered to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Dunhuang prefect Yao Jing and Jinchang prefect Li Chun handed over their commanderies to Lü Guang.

sentences.zh: 胤及光戰于安彌，為光所敗。

translations.literal: Yin and Guang fought at Anmi; he was defeated by Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin met Lü Guang at Anmi and was routed.

sentences.zh: 武威太守彭濟執熙迎光，光殺之。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Wuwei, Peng Ji, seized Xi and welcomed Guang; Guang killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei prefect Peng Ji seized Liang Xi to welcome Lü Guang, who then put Liang Xi to death.

sentences.zh: 建威、西郡太守索泮，奮威、督洪池已南諸軍事、酒泉太守宋皓等，並為光所殺。

translations.literal: The General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of the Western Commandery, Suo Pan; the General Who Rouses Might and Supervisor of Military Affairs South of Hongchi Pool, Administrator of Jiuquan Song Hao, and others, all were killed by Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Pan, general who establishes might and western commandery prefect, and Song Hao, general who rouses might, military overseer south of Hongchi, and Jiuquan prefect, among others, were all executed by Lü Guang.

sentences.zh: 堅尚書令、魏昌公苻纂自關中來奔，拜太尉，進封東海王。

translations.literal: Jian's Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Weichang Fu Zuan, came fleeing from Guanzhong; he was appointed Grand Commandant and advanced enfeoffment to Prince of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan, Fu Jian’s chief minister and Duke of Weichang, fled from Guanzhong to join Fu Pi and was named grand commandant and Prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 以中山太守王兗為平東將軍、平州刺史、阜城侯，苻定為征東將軍、冀州牧、高城侯，苻紹為鎮東將軍、督冀州諸軍事、重合侯，苻謨為征西將軍、幽州牧、高邑侯，苻亮為鎮北大將軍、督幽、并二州諸軍事，並進爵郡公。

translations.literal: He appointed the Administrator of Zhongshan, Wang Yan, General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Ping, Marquis of Fucheng; Fu Ding General Who Conquers the East, Governor of Ji, Marquis of Gaocheng; Fu Shao General Who Guards the East, Supervisor of Military Affairs of Ji, Marquis of Chonghe; Fu Mo General Who Conquers the West, Governor of You, Marquis of Gaoyi; Fu Liang General Who Guards the North, Supervisor of Military Affairs of You and Bing—all advanced in noble rank to Dukes of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan prefect Wang Yan became general who pacifies the east, Pingzhou inspector, and Marquis of Fucheng; Fu Ding was named general who conquers the east and Ji governor as Marquis of Gaocheng; Fu Shao became general who guards the east and Ji theater commander as Marquis of Chonghe; Fu Mo took general who conquers the west and You governor as Marquis of Gaoyi; Fu Liang became supreme northern commander for You and Bing; each was promoted to commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 定、紹據信都，謨、亮先據常山，慕容垂之圍鄴城也，並降于垂，聞丕稱尊號，遣使謝罪。

translations.literal: Ding and Shao held Xindu; Mo and Liang first held Changshan; when Murong Chui besieged Ye city, they all surrendered to Chui; hearing Pi assumed the exalted title, they dispatched envoys apologizing for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ding and Fu Shao held Xindu while Fu Mo and Fu Liang had occupied Changshan; during Murong Chui’s siege of Ye they had all submitted to him, but when they learned that Fu Pi had taken the throne they sent envoys to apologize.

sentences.zh: 王兗固守博陵，與垂相持。

translations.literal: Wang Yan firmly guarded Boling and faced off against Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan held Boling in a stubborn standoff with Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 左將軍竇沖、秦州刺史王統、河州刺史毛興、益州刺史王廣、南秦州刺史楊璧、衛將軍楊定，並據隴右，遣使招丕，請討姚萇。

translations.literal: General of the Left Dou Chong, Inspector of Qin Wang Tong, Inspector of He Mao Xing, Inspector of Yi Wang Guang, Inspector of South Qin Yang Bi, General of the Guard Yang Ding—all held Longyou, dispatched envoys to summon Pi, and requested to attack Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Left general Dou Chong, Qinzhou inspector Wang Tong, Hezhou inspector Mao Xing, Yizhou inspector Wang Guang, southern Qinzhou inspector Yang Bi, and guard general Yang Ding all controlled Longyou; they sent envoys urging Fu Pi to join them in a campaign against Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 丕大悅，以定為驃騎大將軍、雍州牧，沖為征西大將軍、梁州牧，統鎮西大將軍，興車騎大將軍，璧征南大將軍，並開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍，廣安西將軍，皆進位州牧。

translations.literal: Pi was greatly pleased; he appointed Ding General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Yong, Chong General Who Conquers the West and Governor of Liang, Tong General Who Guards the West, Xing General of Chariots and Cavalry, Bi General Who Conquers the South—all opened offices with ceremonies equal to the Three Offices, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Guang General Who Pacifies the West—all advanced position to Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi was delighted: Yang Ding became grand general of agile cavalry and Yongzhou governor; Dou Chong general who conquers the west and Liangzhou governor; Wang Tong general who guards the west; Mao Xing general of chariots and cavalry; Yang Bi general who conquers the south—each received an independent command equal to the three dukes, the cavalier attendant title, Wang Guang the general who pacifies the west, and all were elevated to provincial governor rank.

sentences.zh: 於是王永宣檄州郡曰：「大行皇帝棄背萬國，四海無主。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Yong proclaimed to the provinces and commanderies, saying: "The greatly proceeding emperor has abandoned and turned his back on the myriad states; within the four seas there is no lord.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong then issued a manifesto to every province and commandery: “The late emperor has left the realm, and no sovereign holds the allegiance of the land.”

sentences.zh: 征東大將軍、長樂公，先帝元子，聖武自天，受命荊南，威振衡海，分陝東都，道被夷夏，仁澤光於宇宙，德聽侔于《下武》。

translations.literal: The General Who Conquers the East, Duke of Changle, the Former Emperor's eldest son by the principal consort, sagely martial from Heaven, received mandate south of Jing, awe shakes Heng and sea, divided Shan east capital, his way covers Yi and Xia, humane grace shines through the cosmos, virtue's hearing equals the "Lower Martial."
translations.idiomatic: The general who conquers the east and Duke of Changle—the late emperor’s eldest son—is heaven-endowed with martial sagehood; invested south of the Jing, his majesty rolls from the Heng region to the sea; like the kings who split the realm east of Shan, his influence spans barbarian and Chinese; his kindness fills the cosmos, and his virtue rivals the ode ‘Lower Martial.’”

sentences.zh: 永與司空蠔等謹順天人之望，以季秋吉辰奉公紹承大統，銜哀即事，棲穀總戎，枕戈待旦，志雪大恥。

translations.literal: Yong and Minister of Works Hao and others carefully followed Heaven and men's hopes; on an auspicious day of late autumn they reverently presented the Duke to inherit the great succession; bearing grief they took up affairs, dwelt on coarse grain and commanded weapons, pillow spear awaiting dawn, intending to wash away the great shame.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong and Minister of Works Zhang Hao, deferring to heaven and popular sentiment, on an auspicious autumn day invested the duke as heir to the throne; heartsick yet resolute, they tightened their belts, took command of the armies, slept with weapons at hand, and swore to erase this national humiliation.”

sentences.zh: 慕容垂為封豕於關東，泓、沖繼凶於京邑，致乘輿播越，宗社淪傾。

translations.literal: Murong Chui became a great boar in Guandong; Hong and Chong continued fierceness in the capital region, causing the imperial carriage to be driven about and the ancestral altars to sink and overturn.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui rampages through the lands east of the passes like a monstrous boar; Fu Hong and Fu Chong have carried slaughter into the capital until the throne is driven into exile and the dynastic shrines lie in ruins.”

sentences.zh: 羌賊姚萇，我之牧士，乘釁滔天，親行大逆，有生之巨賊也。

translations.literal: The Qiang bandit Yao Chang, our shepherd officer, riding on the crack swallows Heaven, personally enacted great rebellion—among the living he is a great villain.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang rebel Yao Chang—once a herdsman on our payroll—has exploited turmoil to tower above heaven itself and has personally committed the gravest treason; he is the greatest villain alive.”

sentences.zh: 永累葉受恩，世荷將相，不與驪山之戎、滎澤之狄共戴皇天，同履厚土。

translations.literal: Yong for accumulated generations has received favor; generations have borne general and minister; he does not together with the Rong of Mount Li and the Di of Yingze wear the August Heaven or tread the thick earth.
translations.idiomatic: My house has enjoyed imperial favor for generations and worn ministerial ribbons age after age—I will not share heaven and earth with the savages of Mount Li or the barbarians of Ying marsh.”

sentences.zh: 諸牧伯公侯或宛沛宗臣，或四七勳舊，豈忍舍破國之醜豎，縱殺君之逆賊乎！

translations.literal: The various shepherds, counts, dukes, and marquises are either Wan and Pei lineage ministers or four-seven merit elders—how could they bear to abandon the ugly brats who destroyed the state and indulge the rebellious villains who killed the lord!
translations.idiomatic: You governors and nobles—some kin to the imperial clan at Wan and Pei, some veterans of four generations of service—can you truly stomach sheltering the wretches who shattered the realm or indulging the traitors who murdered their sovereign?”

sentences.zh: 主上飛龍九五，實協天心，靈祥休瑞，史不輟書，投戈效義之士三十餘萬，少康、光武之功可旬朔而成。

translations.literal: The lord above flies dragon on the fifth and ninth; truly he harmonizes Heaven's heart; auspicious omens and felicitous signs, history does not cease writing; men who cast aside spears and devote to righteousness are more than three hundred thousand; the merit of Shaokang and Guangwu can be completed in a ten-day month.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign has mounted the throne as the true dragon; omens crowd the chronicles without cease; more than three hundred thousand warriors have thrown down their arms to rally to justice—the restoration won by Shaokang or Guangwu can be ours within weeks.”

sentences.zh: 今以衛將軍俱石子為前軍師，司空張蠔為中軍都督。

translations.literal: Now taking General of the Guard Ju Shizi as Forward Army Mentor, Minister of Works Zhang Hao as Central Army Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: General of the guard Ju Shizi is appointed mentor of the vanguard; Minister of Works Zhang Hao commands the central army.”

sentences.zh: 武將猛士，風烈雷震，志殄元凶，義無他顧。

translations.literal: Military generals and fierce warriors, wind fierce thunder shake, intending to exterminate the chief culprit, in righteousness there is no other looking.
translations.idiomatic: Our fierce hosts move like wind and thunder; they mean to crush the arch-traitor and will look to nothing else until duty is done.”

sentences.zh: 永謹奉乘輿，恭行天罰。

translations.literal: Yong reverently upholds the imperial carriage and respectfully carries out Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong reverently attends the imperial carriage and carries out heaven’s judgment upon the rebels.”

sentences.zh: 君臣終始之義，在三忘軀之誠，戮力同之，以建晉、鄭之美。」

translations.literal: The righteousness of lord and minister from beginning to end; the sincerity of forgetting one's body in the three [bonds]; join strength together with it, to establish the beauty of Jin and Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: Let lord and ministers uphold their covenant unto death; let every loyal breast forget self as the three bonds demand; together we shall strive as Duke Wen of Jin and Duke Zhuang of Zheng once did.”

sentences.zh: 先是，慕容驎攻王兗於博陵，至是糧竭矢盡，郡功曹張猗逾城聚眾應驎。

translations.literal: Earlier, Murong Lin attacked Wang Yan at Boling; by this time grain was exhausted and arrows were spent; the Commandery Merit Clerk Zhang Yi climbed over the wall and gathered multitudes to respond to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin had long besieged Wang Yan at Boling; supplies and arrows were gone when merit clerk Zhang Yi slipped over the walls and rallied townsmen to open the gates for Lin.

sentences.zh: 袞臨城數之曰：「卿，秦之人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yan approached the wall and rebuked him, saying: "You are a man of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan leaned from the battlements and rebuked him: “You are a subject of Qin.

sentences.zh: 吾，卿之君也。

translations.literal: I am your lord.
translations.idiomatic: I am your lord.

sentences.zh: 起眾應賊，號稱義兵，何名實相違之甚！

translations.literal: You raised multitudes to respond to bandits, calling them righteous troops—how extremely name and reality contradict!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you raise militia for rebels and call it righteousness—how twisted your words and deeds have become!”

sentences.zh: 卿兄往合鄉宗，親逐城主，天地不容，為世大戮。

translations.literal: Your elder brother formerly united township lineage and personally drove out the city lord—Heaven and Earth could not contain him; he received great execution from the age.
translations.idiomatic: Your elder brother once rallied the countryside, drove out the prefect, and earned heaven’s wrath—he was executed as a public criminal.

sentences.zh: 身滅未幾，卿復續之。

translations.literal: His body was extinguished not long ago; you again continue it.
translations.idiomatic: His corpse is barely cold and you repeat his crime.

sentences.zh: 卿見為吾吏，親尋干戈，競為戎首，為爾君者，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: You see you are my officer, yet personally seek spears and shields, competing to be war leader—for one who is your lord, is it not also difficult!
translations.idiomatic: You serve under my banner yet take up arms and lead the mutiny—what lord could endure such a vassal?”

sentences.zh: 今人何取卿一切之功，寧能忘卿不忠不孝之事！

translations.literal: Now people how take your mere merit—can they forget your unfilial and disloyal deeds!
translations.idiomatic: Do you think anyone will praise your petty deeds and forget disloyalty to your ruler and cruelty to your kin?”

sentences.zh: 古人有雲，求忠臣必出孝子之門，卿母在城，不能顧之，何忠義之可望！

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: seeking loyal ministers surely comes from filial sons' gates; your mother is in the city and you cannot care for her—what loyalty and righteousness can be hoped!
translations.idiomatic: The elders said loyal ministers come only from filial homes—your mother remains inside these walls and you abandon her; where is your loyalty or duty?”

sentences.zh: 惡不絕世，卿之謂也。

translations.literal: Evil does not cut off from the generation—this refers to you.
translations.idiomatic: Villainy runs in families, and yours proves the proverb.”

sentences.zh: 不圖中州禮義之邦邦，而卿門風若斯。

translations.literal: I did not scheme that in the Central Plain's courtesy and righteousness state-state, yet your gate's wind is like this.
translations.idiomatic: I never imagined such conduct could come from a house in the heartland of ritual.”

sentences.zh: 卿去老母如脫屣，吾復何論哉！

translations.literal: You discard your old mother like casting off sandals—what more can I discuss!
translations.idiomatic: You cast off your aged mother like a worn shoe—why waste words on you?”

sentences.zh: 」既而城陷，兗及固安侯苻鑒，並為驎所殺。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the city fell; Wang Yan and Marquis of Gu'an Fu Jian were both killed by Lin.
translations.idiomatic: ” Soon the city fell; Wang Yan and Marquis of Gu’an Fu Jian were both put to death by Murong Lin.

sentences.zh: 丕復以王永為司徒、錄尚書事，徐義為尚書令，加右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Pi again appointed Wang Yong Minister of Education and Recorder of Masters of Writing Affairs, Xu Yi Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, adding Right Grand Master of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi again named Wang Yong minister of education with supervisory power over the secretariat; Xu Yi became chief minister of the secretariat with the additional title of right grand master of imperial entertainments.

sentences.zh: 初，王廣還自成都也，奔其兄秦州刺史統。

translations.literal: Initially, when Wang Guang returned from Chengdu, he fled to his elder brother the Inspector of Qin, Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Guang withdrew from Chengdu, he threw himself on his brother Wang Tong, governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 及長安不守，廣攻河州牧毛興於枹罕。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was not kept, Guang attacked He Governor Mao Xing at Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang’an fell, Wang Guang attacked Hezhou governor Mao Xing at Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 興遣建節將軍、臨清柏衛平率其宗人千七百夜擊廣軍，大敗之。

translations.literal: Xing dispatched the General Who Establishes Order, Bai Weiping of Linqing, leading his lineage men seventeen hundred to strike Guang's army by night and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xing sent general who establishes integrity Bai Weiping of Linqing with seventeen hundred clansmen in a night attack that shattered Wang Guang’s army.

sentences.zh: 王統復遣兵助廣，興於是嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Wang Tong again dispatched troops to aid Guang; Xing thereupon encircled the city and firmly guarded.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong sent reinforcements, so Mao Xing drew up his bridges and held Fuhan behind closed gates.

sentences.zh: 既而襲王廣，敗之，廣亡奔秦州，為隴西鮮卑匹蘭所執，送詣姚萇。

translations.literal: Afterward he attacked Wang Guang, defeated him; Guang fled in defeat to Qinzhou, was seized by the Xianbei Pilan of Longxi, and sent to Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon ambushed Wang Guang, routed him, and drove him toward Qinzhou, where Longxi Xianbei chief Pilan seized him and handed him over to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 興既敗王廣，謀伐王統，平上邽。

translations.literal: Xing having defeated Wang Guang, plotted to attack Wang Tong and pacify Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: After beating Wang Guang, Mao Xing planned to march on Wang Tong and secure Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 袍罕諸氐皆窘於兵革而疲不堪命，乃殺興，推衛平為使持節、安西將軍、河州刺史，遣使請命。

translations.literal: The various Di of Fuhan were all distressed by weapons and armor and weary beyond bearing orders; thereupon they killed Xing, promoted Weiping as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of He, and dispatched envoys requesting mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The Di clans of Fuhan, exhausted by endless war, slew Mao Xing and elevated Wei Ping to staff-bearing general who pacifies the west and Hezhou inspector, then sought Fu Pi’s confirmation.

sentences.zh: 刁雲殺慕容忠，乃推慕容永為使持節、大都督中外諸軍事、大將軍、大單于、雍、秦、梁、涼四州牧、錄尚書事、河東王、稱籓於垂。

translations.literal: Diao Yun killed Murong Zhong; thereupon they promoted Murong Yong as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, Governor of Yong, Qin, Liang, and Liang Four Provinces, Recorder of Masters of Writing Affairs, Prince of Hedong, declaring vassalage to Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yun murdered Murong Zhong, then raised Murong Yong with staff authority as supreme commander, grand general and great chanyu, governor of Yong, Qin, Liang province (upper Han basin), and Hexi Liangzhou, chief minister, Prince of Hedong, nominally subordinate to Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 征東苻定、鎮東苻紹、征北苻謨、鎮北苻亮皆降于慕容垂。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the East Fu Ding, General Who Guards the East Fu Shao, General Who Conquers the North Fu Mo, General Who Guards the North Fu Liang all surrendered to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ding, Fu Shao, Fu Mo, and Fu Liang—the eastern and northern commanders—each capitulated to Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 丕又進王永為左丞相，苻纂為大司馬，張蠔為太尉，王騰為驃騎大將軍、儀同三司，徐義為司空，苻沖為車騎大將軍、尚書令、儀同三司，俱石子為衛大將軍、尚書左僕射，領官皆如故。

translations.literal: Pi again advanced Wang Yong to Left Chancellor, Fu Zuan to Grand Marshal, Zhang Hao to Grand Commandant, Wang Teng to General of Agile Cavalry with ceremonies equal to Three Offices, Xu Yi to Minister of Works, Fu Chong to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Supervisor of Masters of Writing, ceremonies equal to Three Offices, Ju Shizi to Grand General of the Guard, Left Vice Director of Masters of Writing; concurrent offices all as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi promoted Wang Yong to left chancellor, Fu Zuan to grand marshal, Zhang Hao to grand commandant, Wang Teng to grand general of agile cavalry with three-duke privileges, Xu Yi to minister of works, Fu Chong to chief minister and general of chariots and cavalry with three-duke privileges, Ju Shizi to guard general and senior vice minister—each kept his other posts.

sentences.zh: 永又檄州郡曰：「昔夏有窮夷之難，少康起焉；

translations.literal: Yong again proclaimed to the provinces and commanderies, saying: "Formerly Xia had the distress of Youqiong Yi; Shaokang arose thereupon;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong issued another circular: “When the Xia court faced the Youqiong crisis, Shaokang restored the line;

sentences.zh: 王莽毒殺平帝，世祖重光漢道；

translations.literal: Wang Mang poison-killed Emperor Ping; the Shizu restored brilliance to the Han way;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang murdered Emperor Ping, yet Emperor Guangwu relit the Han flame;

sentences.zh: 百六之運，何代無之！

translations.literal: The hundred-six fate—what generation lacks it!
translations.idiomatic: Every dynasty knows its share of catastrophic cycles.

sentences.zh: 天降喪亂，羌胡猾夏，先帝晏駕賊庭，京師鞠為戎穴，神州蕭條，生靈塗炭。

translations.literal: Heaven sent down mourning and chaos; Qiang and Hu misled Xia; the Former Emperor expired in the bandit court; the capital region became entirely a barbarian den; the divine land is desolate; the living kind smeared in charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has sent calamity: Qiang and Hu trample the Chinese heartland, our late sovereign died in rebel hands, the capital has become a barbarian warren, and the Central Plain lies in ashes.

sentences.zh: 天未亡秦，社稷有奉。

translations.literal: Heaven has not yet extinguished Qin; the altars of soil and grain have one who receives them.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is not finished with Great Qin—the altars of state still have rightful heirs.

sentences.zh: 主上聖德恢弘，道侔光武，所在宅心，天人歸屬，必當隆中興之功，復配天之美。

translations.literal: The lord above's sagely virtue is vast and great; his way equals Guangwu; wherever located they lodge heart; Heaven and men attach—surely he will elevate middle revival's merit and restore matching Heaven's beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign’s virtue is boundless and his mandate rivals Guangwu’s; men and heaven alike turn to him, and he will surely achieve a restoration worthy of the founders.”

sentences.zh: 姚萇殘虐，慕容垂凶暴，所過滅戶夷煙，毀發丘墓，毒遍存亡，痛纏幽顯，雖黃巾之害於九州，赤眉之暴于四海，方之未為甚也。

translations.literal: Yao Chang is cruel and murderous; Murong Chui is fierce and violent; wherever they pass they extinguish households and level smoke, destroy and dig up mounds and tombs; poison spreads through the living and dead; pain binds hidden and manifest; although the Yellow Turbans' harm in the Nine Provinces, the Red Eyebrows' violence in the four seas—compared to them it is not yet extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang is savage and Murong Chui ruthless: where they march they slaughter households and smoke out villages, break open tombs, and poison living and dead alike—anguish runs through this world and the next. Not even the Yellow Turbans or Red Eyebrows matched such cruelty.”

sentences.zh: 今素秋將及，行師令辰，公侯牧守，壘主鄉豪，或戮力國家，乃心王室，各率所統，以孟冬上旬會大駕于臨晉。

translations.literal: Now plain autumn will arrive; marching troops auspicious hour—dukes, marquises, shepherds, guards, fort masters, township heroes—some join strength for the state; hearts are for the royal house—each lead what they command; on the first ten days of the first winter month assemble the great carriage at Linjin.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn draws near—the season to march. Dukes, governors, garrison chiefs, and local magnates who still love the dynasty shall bring their hosts to Linjin in the first tenday of winter to join the imperial campaign.”

sentences.zh: 」於是天水姜延、馮翊寇明、河東王昭、新平張晏、京兆杜敏、扶風馬郎、建忠高平牧官都尉王敏等咸承檄起兵，各有眾數萬，遣使應丕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Jiang Yan of Tianshui, Kou Ming of Fengyi, Wang Zhao of Hedong, Zhang Yan of Xinping, Du Min of Jingzhao, Ma Lang of Fufeng, Wang Min shepherd-official commandant of Gaoping of Jianzhong and others all received the proclamation and raised troops; each had multitudes of several tens of thousands; dispatched envoys responding to Pi.
translations.idiomatic: ” Thereupon Jiang Yan of Tianshui, Kou Ming of Fengyi, Wang Zhao of Hedong, Zhang Yan of Xinping, Du Min of Jingzhao, Ma Lang of Fufeng, Wang Min of the Jianzhong gaoping pasture command, and others rose at the summons, each commanding tens of thousands, and sent envoys to Fu Pi.

sentences.zh: 皆就拜將軍、郡守，封列侯。

translations.literal: All were then appointed generals and administrators, enfeoffed as marquises of lie.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi commissioned them as generals and prefects and invested them as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 冠軍鄧景擁眾五千據彭池，與竇沖為首尾，擊萇平涼太守金熙。

translations.literal: Champion Deng Jing grasped multitudes five thousand and held Pengchi, with Dou Chong as head and tail, attacked Chang's Administrator of Pingliang, Jin Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Champion general Deng Jing held Peng Pool with five thousand men, coordinated with Dou Chong in a pincer, and struck Pingliang prefect Jin Xi, who served Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 安定北部都尉鮮卑沒奕於率鄯善王胡員吒、護羌中郎將梁苟奴等，與萇左將軍姚方成、鎮遠強京戰于孫丘谷，大敗之。

translations.literal: The Northern Commandant of Anding, Xianbei Moyigan, leading the King of Shanshan Hu Yuanzha, the Colonel Protecting the Qiang Liang Gounu, and others, together with Chang's Left General Yao Fangcheng and the General Who Guards the Distance Qiang Jing, fought at Sunqiu Valley and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The northern commandant of Anding, the Xianbei chief Moyigan, at the head of the king of Shanshan Hu Yuanzha, colonel protecting the Qiang Liang Gounu, and others, met Yao Chang’s left general Yao Fangcheng and general who guards the distance Qiang Jing at Sunqiu Valley and routed them.

sentences.zh: 枹罕諸氐以衛平年老，不可以成事業，議廢之，而憚其宗強，連日不決。

translations.literal: The various Di of Fuhan considered Wei Ping old and unable to complete enterprises; they deliberated deposing him but feared his lineage's strength; day after day they did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The Di clans at Fuhan judged Wei Ping too old to finish what they had begun and debated replacing him, yet they dreaded his clan’s power and put off a decision day after day.

sentences.zh: 氐有啖青者，謂諸將曰：「大事宜定，東討姚萇，不可沈吟猶豫。

translations.literal: Among the Di was one Dan Qing, who said to the various generals: "Great matters ought to be settled; east we attack Yao Chang—one cannot sink in hesitation and doubt.
translations.idiomatic: A Di leader named Dan Qing told the commanders, “We must settle policy at once and march east against Yao Chang—there is no room for endless hesitation.”

sentences.zh: 一旦事發，反為人害。

translations.literal: Once the affair breaks out, on the contrary one becomes harmed by others.
translations.idiomatic: If we delay until crisis strikes, we ourselves will be destroyed.”

sentences.zh: 諸軍但請衛公會儲眾將，青為諸軍決之。

translations.literal: The various armies only request Duke Wei to assemble and store the gathered generals; Qing will decide it for the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Summon Duke Wei to meet every commander in council—I will settle the matter for the host.”

sentences.zh: 」眾以為然。

translations.literal: " The multitude deemed it so.
translations.idiomatic: ” The officers agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是大饗諸將，青抽劍而前曰：「今天下大亂，豺狼塞路，吾曹今日可謂休戚是同，非賢明之主莫可濟艱難也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly feasted the various generals; Qing drew his sword and stepped forward, saying: "Now the realm is greatly chaotic; wolves and jackals block the roads; we today can be called sharing sorrow and joy—without an enlightened lord none can ford hardship.
translations.idiomatic: They held a grand banquet where Dan Qing stepped forward with drawn sword and said, “The empire lies in ruins and predators choke every road; we share one fortune now, yet only a worthy sovereign can carry us through.”

sentences.zh: 衛公朽耄，不足以成大事，宜反初服，以避賢路，狄道長苻登雖王室疏屬，而志略雄明，請共立之，以赴大駕。

translations.literal: Duke Wei is rotten and aged, insufficient to complete great matters; it is fitting to return to initial garments to yield the worthy road; the Magistrate of Didao, Fu Deng, although a distant kin of the royal house, has heroic and bright ambition and strategy—please jointly establish him to go to the great carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wei is enfeebled and cannot bear the burden—let him step aside for worthier men. Fu Deng of Didao, though a distant imperial clansman, is bold and astute; elevate him together so we may rally to the true emperor.”

sentences.zh: 諸君若有不同者，便下異議。

translations.literal: If among you gentlemen there are those who disagree, then present differing proposals.
translations.idiomatic: If any of you dissent, speak now.”

sentences.zh: 」乃奮劍攘袂，將斬貳己者，眾皆從之，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he brandished his sword and pushed back his sleeves, about to behead those doubly against himself; the multitude all followed him; none dared look up.
translations.idiomatic: ” He raised his blade and bared his arm, ready to strike down anyone who hesitated; the assembly yielded and no one met his eye.

sentences.zh: 於是推登為帥，遣使於丕請命。

translations.literal: Thereupon they promoted Deng as commander and dispatched envoys to Pi requesting mandate.
translations.idiomatic: They acclaimed Fu Deng as leader and sent envoys to Fu Pi asking imperial confirmation.

sentences.zh: 丕以登為征西大將軍、開府儀同三司、南安王、持節及州郡督因其所稱而授之。

translations.literal: Pi appointed Deng General Who Conquers the West, opened office with ceremonies equal to Three Offices, Prince of Nan'an, Bearer of Staff—and provincial and commandery supervisors according to what they had styled themselves he conferred.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi named Fu Deng general who conquers the west with independent command matching the three dukes, Prince of Nan’an, and invested him with the imperial staff; provincial titles followed the ranks his followers already claimed.

sentences.zh: 又以徐義為右丞相。

translations.literal: He also appointed Xu Yi Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yi was appointed right chancellor.

sentences.zh: 丕留王騰守晉陽，楊輔戍壺關，率眾四萬進據平陽。

translations.literal: Pi left Wang Teng to defend Jinyang, Yang Fu to garrison Huguan, led forty thousand multitudes forward and occupied Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi left Wang Teng to hold Jinyang and Yang Fu to guard Huguan while he marched forty thousand men into Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 王統以秦州降姚萇。

translations.literal: Wang Tong with Qin surrendered to Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong surrendered Qinzhou to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 慕容永以丕至平陽，恐不自固，乃遣使求假道還東，丕弗許。

translations.literal: Murong Yong because Pi arrived at Pingyang, feared he could not secure himself; thereupon dispatched envoys requesting borrowed passage to return east; Pi did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong trembled when Fu Pi reached Pingyang and begged permission to march east through Fu Pi’s lines; Fu Pi refused.

sentences.zh: 遣王永及苻纂攻之，以俱石子為前鋒都督，與慕容永戰於襄陵。

translations.literal: He dispatched Wang Yong and Fu Zuan to attack him, appointing Ju Shizi Forward Vanguard Supervisor; they fought Murong Yong at Xiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi sent Wang Yong and Fu Zuan against him with Ju Shizi leading the van; they met Murong Yong at Xiangling.

sentences.zh: 王永大敗，永及石子皆死之。

translations.literal: Wang Yong was greatly defeated; Yong and Shizi both died therein.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong suffered a crushing defeat; both he and Ju Shizi fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 初，苻纂之奔丕也，部下壯士三千餘人，丕猜而忌之。

translations.literal: Initially, when Fu Zuan fled to Pi, his subordinate stalwart soldiers were more than three thousand; Pi suspected and envied him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Zuan first joined Fu Pi he brought three thousand picked warriors, and Fu Pi regarded him with jealousy and mistrust.

sentences.zh: 及永之敗，懼為纂所殺，率騎數千南奔東垣。

translations.literal: When Yong was defeated, he feared being killed by Zuan; leading several thousand cavalry he fled south to Dongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Yong’s defeat Fu Pi feared Fu Zuan might kill him and fled south toward Dongyuan with thousands of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 晉揚威將軍馮該自陝要擊，敗之，斬丕首，執其太子甯、長樂王壽，送于京師，朝廷赦而不誅，歸之於苻宏。

translations.literal: Jin's General Who Displays Might Feng Gai from Shan intercepted and struck him, defeated him, beheaded Pi, seized his heir apparent Ning and Prince of Changle Shou, sent them to the capital court; the court pardoned and did not execute, returning them to Fu Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Jin general Feng Gai ambushed him at Shan, took Fu Pi’s head, and captured the heir Fu Ning and Prince of Changle Fu Shou; the eastern court spared them and handed them to Fu Hong.

sentences.zh: 徐義為慕容永所獲，械埋其足，將殺之。

translations.literal: Xu Yi was captured by Murong Yong; shackled with buried feet; about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong seized Xu Yi, clamped his legs in stocks buried in the earth, and prepared to execute him.

sentences.zh: 義誦《觀世音經》，至夜中，土開械脫，於重禁之中若有人導之者，遂奔楊佺期，佺期以為洛陽令。

translations.literal: Yi recited the Guanshiyin sutra; reaching midnight, earth opened the shackles and released; in heavy prohibition within it was as if someone guided him; thereupon he fled to Yang Quanqi; Quanqi appointed him Luoyang Magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yi chanted the Avalokiteśvara scripture until at midnight the earth loosened his fetters and he slipped from prison as though guided by a spirit; he escaped to Yang Quanqi, who named him magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 苻纂及弟師奴率丕余眾數萬，奔據杏城。

translations.literal: Fu Zuan and younger brother Shinu led Pi's remaining multitudes of several tens of thousands, fled and occupied Xingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan and his brother Shinu led tens of thousands of Fu Pi’s survivors to seize Xingcheng.

sentences.zh: 苻登稱尊號，偽諡丕為哀平皇帝。

translations.literal: Fu Deng assumed the exalted title; falsely posthumously titled Pi as Emperor Aiping.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Deng took the throne he posthumously honored Fu Pi as Emperor Aiping.

sentences.zh: 丕之臣佐皆沒慕容永，永乃進據上党之長子，僭稱大號，改元曰中興。

translations.literal: Pi's ministers and aides all fell to Murong Yong; Yong thereupon advanced and occupied Changzi of Shangdang, arrogated the great title, changed era name to Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong absorbed Fu Pi’s officials, seized Changzi in Shangdang, proclaimed his own dynasty, and adopted the era name Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 丕在位二年而敗。

translations.literal: Pi was on the throne two years and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi reigned two years before ruin overtook him.

sentences.zh: 登字文高，堅之族孫也。

translations.literal: Deng, courtesy name Wengao, was a lineage grandson of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng, courtesy name Wengao, was a distant kinsman of Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 父敞，健之世為太尉司馬、隴東太守、建節將軍，後為苻生所殺。

translations.literal: Father Chang, in Jian's age was Grand Commandant Major, Administrator of Longdong, General Who Establishes Order; afterward was killed by Fu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu Chang had served Fu Jiàn as grand commandant’s aide, Longdong prefect, and general who establishes integrity until Fu Sheng executed him.

sentences.zh: 堅即偽位，追贈右將軍、涼州刺史，以登兄同成嗣。

translations.literal: When Jian assumed the false position, posthumously gifted Right General, Inspector of Liang; letting Deng's elder brother Tongcheng inherit.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian took the throne he posthumously named Fu Chang general of the right and Liangzhou inspector, with succession passing to Fu Deng’s elder brother Fu Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 毛興之鎮上邽，以為長史。

translations.literal: When Mao Xing garrisoned Shanggui, he appointed him Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao Xing governed Shanggui he named Fu Deng his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 登少而雄勇，有壯氣，粗險不修細行，故堅弗之奇也。

translations.literal: Deng from youth was heroic and brave, had stalwart qi, rough and perilous, not cultivating small conduct; therefore Jian did not deem him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng was fierce and daring in youth but coarse and careless of etiquette, so Fu Jian never singled him out.

sentences.zh: 長而折節謹厚，頗覽書傳。

translations.literal: Grown, he bent his measure and was cautious and thick; broadly perused documents and traditions.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he curbed his temper, grew conscientious, and read widely.

sentences.zh: 拜殿上將軍，稍遷羽林監、揚武將軍、長安令，坐事黜為狄道長。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace General, gradually promoted to Commandant of the Feathered Forest, General Who Displays Might, Magistrate of Chang'an; sitting on an affair was demoted to Magistrate of Didao.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from palace guard to feathered-forest commandant, general who displays might, and magistrate of Chang’an, then was demoted to magistrate of Didao after an offense.

sentences.zh: 及關中亂，去縣歸毛興。

translations.literal: When Guanzhong was chaotic, he left the county and returned to Mao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanzhong collapsed he quit his post and joined Mao Xing.

sentences.zh: 同成言於興，請以登為司馬，常在營部。

translations.literal: Tongcheng spoke to Xing, requesting to appoint Deng as Major, constantly in camp headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Tongcheng asked Mao Xing to appoint Fu Deng army marshal and keep him always at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 登度量不群，好為奇略，同成常謂之曰：「汝聞不在其位，不謀其政，無數幹時，將為博識者不許。

translations.literal: Deng's measure was not common; he loved to make unusual stratagems; Tongcheng often said to him: "You have heard 'not in his position, not plan his governance'—without reckoning interfering with the times will by the broadly knowledgeable not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng’s ambitions were unusual and he loved bold schemes; Fu Tongcheng warned him, “You know the saying ‘outside office, mind no policy’—meddling repeatedly will earn censure from men of judgment.”

sentences.zh: 吾非疾汝，恐或不喜人妄豫耳，自是可止。

translations.literal: I am not sick of you; I fear perhaps others do not like people rashly participating—that from this can stop.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I resent you—others dislike unsolicited advice; curb yourself from here on.”

sentences.zh: 汝後得政，自可專意。

translations.literal: When afterward you obtain governance, naturally you can devote intention solely.
translations.idiomatic: When authority is yours, pursue policy as you see fit.”

sentences.zh: 」時人聞同成言，多以為疾登而抑蔽之。

translations.literal: " People of the time hearing Tongcheng's words, mostly thought he despised Deng and suppressed and concealed him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Hearing Tongcheng’s reproof, many assumed he despised Fu Deng and kept him down.

sentences.zh: 登乃屏跡不妄交遊。

translations.literal: Deng thereupon screened his traces and did not rashly associate and roam.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng withdrew from public life and avoided casual company.

sentences.zh: 興有事則召之，戲謂之曰：「小司馬可坐評事。

translations.literal: When Xing had affairs then summoned him, jokingly said to him: "Little Major may sit and judge affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Mao Xing faced a decision he called Fu Deng in jest: “Let our junior marshal hear the case.”

sentences.zh: 」登出言輒析理中，興內服焉，然敬憚而不能委任。

translations.literal: " Deng whenever he spoke analyzed principle hitting the mark; Xing inwardly submitted to him, yet revered and feared him and could not entrust commission.
translations.idiomatic: ” Fu Deng’s opinions invariably hit the mark; Mao Xing inwardly admired him yet feared his brilliance and withheld real responsibility.

sentences.zh: 姚萇作亂，遣其弟碩德率眾伐毛興，相持久之。

translations.literal: Yao Chang raised rebellion, dispatched his younger brother Shuode leading multitudes to attack Mao Xing; they faced off enduring long.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang rebelled he sent his brother Yao Shuode against Mao Xing, and the two sides remained locked in stalemate.

sentences.zh: 興將死，告同成曰：「與卿累年共擊逆羌，事終不克，何恨之深！

translations.literal: Xing about to die, told Tongcheng: "With you for accumulated years together striking the rebellious Qiang; the affair in the end did not overcome—what regret so deep!
translations.idiomatic: As Mao Xing lay dying he told Tongcheng, “For years we hammered the rebel Qiang yet never broke them—how bitter that failure!”

sentences.zh: 可以後事付卿小弟司馬，殄碩德者，必此人也。

translations.literal: You may after affairs entrust to your younger brother the Major; he who exterminates Shuode—surely this man.
translations.idiomatic: Entrust what follows to your younger brother the marshal—only he can destroy Yao Shuode.”

sentences.zh: 卿可換攝司馬事。」

translations.literal: You may exchange and hold Major affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Take his place as marshal yourself.”

sentences.zh: 登既代衛平，遂專統征伐。

translations.literal: Deng having replaced Wei Ping, thereupon solely commanded campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fu Deng succeeded Wei Ping he held sole command of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 是時歲旱眾饑，道殣相望，登每戰殺賊，名為熟食，謂軍人曰：「汝等朝戰，幕便飽肉，何憂於饑！

translations.literal: At this time the year was drought and the multitude hungry; corpses blocking the road mutually gazed; Deng each battle killed bandits, named it cooked food; said to soldiers: "You wait morning battle, evening then full meat—what worry about hunger!
translations.idiomatic: Famine stalked the land while corpses littered the roads; Fu Deng butchered enemy dead after each clash and called the flesh “cooked rations,” telling his troops, “Fight at dawn and feast by dusk—why fear hunger?”

sentences.zh: 」士眾從之，啖死人肉，輒飽健能鬥。

translations.literal: " The soldiers followed him; eating dead men's flesh, always full and stalwart able to fight.
translations.idiomatic: ” The army obeyed: fed on the fallen, they fought with renewed ferocity.

sentences.zh: 姚萇聞之，急召碩德曰：「汝不來，必為苻登所食盡。

translations.literal: Yao Chang hearing this, urgently summoned Shuode, saying: "If you do not come, surely will by Fu Deng be eaten entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang learned this he summoned Yao Shuode in alarm: “If you stay put, Fu Deng will devour you to the last man.”

sentences.zh: 」碩德於是下隴奔萇。

translations.literal: " Shuode thereupon descended Long and fled to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shuode abandoned Long and withdrew to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 及丕敗，丕尚書寇遺奉丕子渤海王懿、濟北王昶自杏城奔登。

translations.literal: When Pi was defeated, Pi's Minister Kou Yi bore Pi's sons Prince of Bohai Yi and Prince of Jibei Chang from Xingcheng fleeing to Deng.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Pi fell, his minister Kou Yi brought Fu Pi’s sons—the princes of Bohai and Jibei—from Xingcheng to Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 登乃具丕死問，於是為丕發喪行服，三軍縞素。

translations.literal: Deng thereupon prepared Pi's death inquiry; thereupon for Pi observed mourning and wore mourning garments; three armies white silk.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng announced Fu Pi’s death, observed mourning in white, and clothed the army in hemp.

sentences.zh: 登請立懿為主，眾咸曰：「渤海王雖先帝之子，然年在幼沖，未堪多難。

translations.literal: Deng requested establishing Yi as lord; the multitude all said: "Though Prince of Bohai is the Former Emperor's son, yet his years are in tender infancy; not able to bear many hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng urged the enthronement of Fu Yi, but the host replied, “The prince of Bohai is the late emperor’s heir yet still a child—he cannot bear these disasters.”

sentences.zh: 國亂而立長君，《春秋》之義也。

translations.literal: When the state is chaotic and establishes an elder lord—this is the Spring and Autumn's meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn approves raising an elder sovereign when the realm is in chaos.”

sentences.zh: 三虜跨僭，寇旅殷強，豺狼梟鏡，舉目而是，自厄運之極，莫甚於斯。

translations.literal: Three barbarians stride usurpation; raiding hosts abundant and strong; wolves jackals owl mirror—lifting eyes thus it is; since extreme ill fortune's utmost, none exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Three usurpers straddle the north, invaders swarm like wolves and owls—never has fate dealt so cruel a blow.”

sentences.zh: 大王挺劍西州，鳳翔秦、隴，偏師暫接，姚萇奔潰，一戰之功，可謂光格天地。

translations.literal: Great King draws sword in western province; phoenix soars Qin and Long; partial army briefly engaged—Yao Chang flees routed; one battle's merit can be called light piercing Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: You drew your sword in Liangzhou and swept Qin and Long; one probing stroke shattered Yao Chang—a single blow whose brilliance fills heaven and earth.”

sentences.zh: 宜龍驤武奮，拯拔舊京，以社稷宗廟為先，不可顧曹臧、吳劄一介微節，以失圖運之機，不建中興之業也。

translations.literal: It is fitting dragon-soaring martial to rouse, rescue and pull out old capital; take altars of soil and grain and ancestral temple as first; cannot heed Cao Zang, Wu Zha one petty integrity—thereby lose charting fate's opportunity, not establish middle revival's enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Rise like a dragon, reclaim the ancient capital, put the altars first—do not imitate Cao Zang or Wu Zha’s petty scruples and miss the hour of restoration.”

sentences.zh: 」登於是乙太元十一年僭即皇帝位，大赦境內，改元曰太初。

translations.literal: " Deng thereupon in eleventh year of Taiyuan arrogated emperor position, greatly pardoned within territory, changed era name to Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: ” Fu Deng therefore proclaimed himself emperor in the eleventh year of Taiyuan (386), declared amnesty, and adopted the era name Taichu.

sentences.zh: 立堅神主於軍中，載以輜軿，羽葆青蓋，車建黃旗，武賁之士三百人以衛之，將戰必告，凡欲所為，啟主而後行。

translations.literal: He established Jian's spirit lord in the army, carried by covered wagon, feather canopy blue cover, chariot raised yellow banner, three hundred fierce warriors to guard it; about to battle always announced; whatever wished to do, opened to the lord then proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: He placed Fu Jian’s spirit tablet in a curtained carriage with feathered canopy and yellow banner, escorted by three hundred guards, and consulted it before every battle or decree.

sentences.zh: 繕甲纂兵，將引師而東，乃告堅神主曰：「維曾孫皇帝臣登，乙太皇帝之靈恭踐寶位。

translations.literal: He repaired armor gathered troops, about to lead army east; then announced to Jian's spirit lord: "As great-grandson emperor subject Deng, by Grand Emperor's spirit respectfully tread precious position.
translations.idiomatic: After arming his host for an eastern march he addressed Fu Jian’s tablet: “Your great-grandson Fu Deng, by your august spirit, ascends the throne.”

sentences.zh: 昔五將之難，賊羌肆害於聖躬，實登之罪也。

translations.literal: Formerly at the Five Generals' calamity, bandit Qiang wantonly harmed the sagely person—truly Deng's crime.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck the Five Garrisons and Qiang rebels struck you down, I failed you—that guilt is mine.”

sentences.zh: 今合義旅，眾余五萬，精甲勁兵，足以立功，年谷豐穰，足以資贍。

translations.literal: Now gathering righteous hosts, multitudes exceed fifty thousand; refined armor crack troops sufficient to establish merit; yearly grain abundant—sufficient to supply provision.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous bands now exceed fifty thousand well-armed soldiers, and the harvest can sustain them—we can strike with force.”

sentences.zh: 即日星言電邁，直造賊庭，奮不顧命，隕越為期，庶上報皇帝酷冤，下雪臣子大恥。

translations.literal: This day star words lightning rush; straight reach bandit court; rouse not sparing life; fall beyond as term—hopefully upward repay emperor cruel wrong; downward wash minister-subjects great shame.
translations.idiomatic: Today we march like lightning straight on the rebel seat; we race toward death if need be to avenge your murder and wipe away our shame as subjects.”

sentences.zh: 惟帝之靈，降監厥誠。

translations.literal: Only the Emperor's spirit—descend and supervise this sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: May your spirit witness our devotion.”

sentences.zh: 」因覷欷流涕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon looked up sighing and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: ” He broke down sobbing.

sentences.zh: 將士莫不悲慟，皆刻鉾鎧為「死休」字，示以戰死為志。

translations.literal: Generals and soldiers none not grieved greatly; all carved spear armor as characters "death rest," showing taking battle death as intent.
translations.idiomatic: The troops wept with him and engraved “fight to the death” on blades and armor.

sentences.zh: 每戰以長槊鉤刃為方圓大陣，知有厚薄，從中分配，故人自為戰，所向無前。

translations.literal: Each battle using long lance hook blades made square-circle great formation; knowing there is thick thin; from middle distribute allocate—therefore men each fought for themselves; wherever faced none before.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he drew up spear squares with hooks, graded their density, and assigned men so each unit fought as one—his formations swept all before them.

sentences.zh: 初，長安之將敗也，堅中壘將軍徐嵩、屯騎校尉胡空各聚眾五千，據險築堡以自固，而受姚萇官爵。

translations.literal: Initially, when Chang'an was about to be defeated, Jian's Central Rampart General Xu Song and Cavalry Camp Colonel Hu Kong each gathered multitudes five thousand, occupied peril and built fort to secure themselves, yet received Yao Chang's offices and noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chang’an fell, Fu Jian’s generals Xu Song and Hu Kong each raised five thousand men, walled upland forts, yet accepted titles from Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 及萇之害堅，嵩等以王禮葬堅於二堡之間。

translations.literal: When Chang harmed Jian, Song and others with kingly ritual buried Jian between the two forts.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Chang murdered Fu Jian they buried him with royal honors between their two redoubts.

sentences.zh: 至是，各率眾降登。

translations.literal: By this time, each led multitudes to surrender to Deng.
translations.idiomatic: They now brought their hosts over to Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 拜嵩鎮軍將軍、雍州刺史，空輔國將軍、京兆尹。

translations.literal: Appointed Song General Who Garrisons the Army, Inspector of Yong; Kong General Who Supports the State, Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Song became general who guards the army and Yongzhou inspector; Hu Kong general who supports the state and governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 登復改葬堅以天子之禮。

translations.literal: Deng again reburied Jian with Son of Heaven's ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng reinterred Fu Jian with full imperial obsequies.

sentences.zh: 又僭立其妻毛氏為皇后，弟懿為皇太弟。

translations.literal: He also arrogantly established his wife Lady Mao as empress, younger brother Yi as imperial younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: He named Lady Mao empress and his brother Fu Yi heir presumptive.

sentences.zh: 遣使拜苻纂為使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、太師，領大司馬，進封魯王，纂弟師奴為撫軍大將軍、并州牧、朔方公。

translations.literal: He dispatched envoys to appoint Fu Zuan Bearer of Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs, Grand Mentor, concurrently Grand Marshal, advanced enfeoffment Prince of Lu; Zuan's younger brother Shinu General Who Pacifies the Army, Inspector of Bing, Duke of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys invested Fu Zuan as grand mentor and supreme commander with staff authority, chief minister, grand marshal, and Prince of Lu; his brother Shinu became grand general who pacifies the army, Bingzhou governor, and Duke of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 纂怒謂使者曰：「渤海王世祖之孫，先帝之子，南安王何由不立而自尊乎？

translations.literal: Zuan angrily said to the envoy: "Prince of Bohai is Shizu's grandson, Former Emperor's son—how does Nan'an King come not to be established yet self-exalt?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan raged at the envoy: “The prince of Bohai is the grandson of Shizu and son of the late emperor—why does Fu Deng seize the throne instead?”

sentences.zh: 」纂長史王旅諫曰：「南安已立，理無中改。

translations.literal: " Zuan's Chief Clerk Wang Lü remonstrated: "Nan'an already established—by principle there is no middle change.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chief clerk Wang Lü urged restraint: “Fu Deng already reigns; the realm cannot endure another reversal.”

sentences.zh: 賊虜未平，不可宗室之中自為仇敵，原大王遠蹤光武推聖公之義，梟二虜之後，徐更圖之。

translations.literal: Bandit barbarians not yet pacified; cannot within the lineage make oneself hostile foes—hope Great King track afar Guangwu pushing Shenggong's righteousness; after beheading two barbarians, slowly further plan it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels still roam—kinsmen must not tear one another apart; imitate Guangwu yielding place to Liu Xuan until the traitors fall, then revisit the question.”

sentences.zh: 」纂乃受命。

translations.literal: " Zuan thereupon received mandate.
translations.idiomatic: ” Fu Zuan accepted the commission.

sentences.zh: 於是貳縣虜帥彭沛谷、屠各董成、張龍世、新平羌雷惡地等盡應之，有眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Er county barbarian chiefs Peng Peigu, Tuge Dong Cheng, Zhang Longshi, Xinping Qiang Le Erdi and others all responded to him; had multitudes over one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal leaders Peng Peigu of Er county, Dong Cheng of the Tuge, Zhang Longshi, and Le Erdi of Xinping answered his call with more than a hundred thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 纂遣師奴攻上郡羌酋金大黑、金洛生，大黑等逆戰，大敗之，斬首五千八百。

translations.literal: Zuan dispatched Shinu to attack Shang commandery Qiang chiefs Jin Dahei and Jin Luosheng; Dahei and others resisted battle; greatly defeated them; beheaded five thousand eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan sent Shinu against Qiang chiefs Jin Dahei and Jin Luosheng in Shang commandery, shattered them, and took five thousand eight hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 登以竇沖為車騎大將軍、南秦州牧，楊定為大將軍、益州牧，楊璧為司空、梁州牧。

translations.literal: Deng appointed Dou Chong General of Chariots and Cavalry, Governor of South Qin; Yang Ding Grand General, Governor of Yi; Yang Bi Minister of Works, Governor of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng named Dou Chong grand general of chariots and cavalry and southern Qinzhou governor; Yang Ding grand general and Yizhou governor; Yang Bi minister of works and Liangzhou governor.

sentences.zh: 苻纂敗姚碩德于涇陽，姚萇自陰密距纂，纂退屯敷陸。

translations.literal: Fu Zuan defeated Yao Shuode at Jingyang; Yao Chang from Yinmi resisted Zuan; Zuan retreated and encamped at Fulu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan defeated Yao Shuode at Jingyang until Yao Chang advanced from Yinmi and forced him back to Fulu.

sentences.zh: 竇沖攻萇汧、雍二城，克之，斬其將軍姚元平、張略等。

translations.literal: Dou Chong attacked Chang's Qian and Yong two cities, overcame them, beheaded their generals Yao Yuanping, Zhang Lüe, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong stormed Yao Chang’s cities of Qian and Yong, killed generals Yao Yuanping and Zhang Lüe, and seized both towns.

sentences.zh: 又與萇戰於汧東，為萇所敗。

translations.literal: Again he fought Chang east of Qian; was defeated by Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Yao Chang again east of the Qian River and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 登次於瓦亭。

translations.literal: Deng halted at Wuting.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng camped at Wuting.

sentences.zh: 萇攻彭沛穀堡，陷之，沛穀奔杏城，萇遷陰密。

translations.literal: Chang attacked Peng Peigu fort, overcame it; Peigu fled to Xingcheng; Chang moved to Yinmi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang stormed Peng Peigu’s fort, drove Peng Peigu back to Xingcheng, and shifted his own headquarters to Yinmi.

sentences.zh: 登征虜、馮翊太守蘭犢率眾二萬自頻陽入于和寧，與苻纂首尾，將圖長安。

translations.literal: Deng's General Who Conquers Captives, Administrator of Fengyi Lan Du led twenty thousand multitudes from Pinyang entered into Heling, with Fu Zuan head and tail, about to plan Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng’s general who conquers captives and Fengyi prefect Lan Du brought twenty thousand men from Pinyang into Heling to coordinate with Fu Zuan and threaten Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 師奴勸其兄纂稱尊號，纂不從，乃殺纂，自立為秦公。

translations.literal: Shinu urged his elder brother Zuan to assume exalted title; Zuan did not follow; thereupon killed Zuan, self-established as Duke of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Shinu urged Fu Zuan to take the throne; when Fu Zuan refused he murdered him and styled himself duke of Qin.

sentences.zh: 蘭犢絕之，皆為姚萇所敗。

translations.literal: Lan Du cut them off; all were defeated by Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Du broke relations with him, and Yao Chang crushed both forces.

sentences.zh: 登進所胡空堡，戎夏歸之者十有餘萬。

translations.literal: Deng advanced to Hu Kong fort; barbarians and Xia who attached to him were more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng advanced into Hu Kong’s fortress and drew more than a hundred thousand followers, Chinese and tribal alike.

sentences.zh: 姚萇遣其將軍姚方成攻陷徐嵩堡，嵩被殺，悉坑戎士。

translations.literal: Yao Chang dispatched his general Yao Fangcheng attacked and overcame Xu Song's fort; Song was killed; all buried alive warrior soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang sent Yao Fangcheng to storm Xu Song’s fort, executed Xu Song, and buried the garrison alive.

sentences.zh: 登率眾下隴入朝那，姚萇據武都相持，累戰互有勝負。

translations.literal: Deng led multitudes descending Long entering Chaona; Yao Chang occupied Wudu facing off; accumulated battles each had victory and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng led his army off Long into Chaona while Yao Chang held Wudu; they skirmished repeatedly with mixed results.

sentences.zh: 登軍中大饑，收葚以供兵士。

translations.literal: In Deng's army great famine; gathered mulberries to supply soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Famine stalked Fu Deng’s camp, and they gathered wild mulberries to feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 立其子崇為皇太子，弁為南安王，尚為北海王。

translations.literal: He established his son Chong as heir apparent, Bian as Prince of Nan'an, Shang as Prince of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: He named his son Fu Chong crown prince, Fu Bian prince of Nan’an, and Fu Shang prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 姚萇退還安定。

translations.literal: Yao Chang retreated returning to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang pulled back to Anding.

sentences.zh: 登就食新平，留其大軍于胡空堡，率騎萬餘圍萇營，四面大哭，哀聲動人。

translations.literal: Deng went to eat at Xinping; left his great army at Hu Kong fort; led more than ten thousand cavalry surrounding Chang's camp; four sides greatly wept; mournful sound moved people.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng foraged at Xinping while his main force held Hu Kong’s fort; he rode out with ten thousand horse, surrounded Yao Chang’s camp, and set the whole army wailing until the sound shook the field.

sentences.zh: 萇惡之，乃命三軍哭以應登，登乃引退。

translations.literal: Chang loathed it; thereupon ordered three armies weep to respond to Deng; Deng thereupon led retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang detested the omen and ordered his own troops to wail in answer; Fu Deng then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 萇以登頻戰輒勝，謂堅有神驗，亦于軍中立堅神主，請曰：「往年新平之禍，非萇之罪。

translations.literal: Chang because Deng frequently battled always victorious, believed Jian had spirit verification; also in army established Jian spirit lord, requesting: "In former years Xinping's calamity was not Chang's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fu Deng kept winning, Yao Chang feared Fu Jian’s ghost and set up his own tablet in camp, pleading, “The tragedy at Xinping was not my doing.”

sentences.zh: 臣兄襄從陝北渡，假路求西，狐死首丘，欲暫見鄉里。

translations.literal: My elder brother Xiang crossed north from Shan, borrowed road seeking west—fox dies head toward mound—wished briefly to see hometown.
translations.idiomatic: My brother Yao Xiang crossed from northern Shan, asked passage westward; like the fox that faces its burrow in death, he longed one glimpse of home.

sentences.zh: 陛下與苻眉要路距擊，不遂而沒。

translations.literal: Your Majesty with Fu Mei at crucial road resisted strike—did not succeed and perished.
translations.idiomatic: You and Fu Mei barred his path; the strike failed and my brother fell.

sentences.zh: 襄敕臣行殺，非臣之罪。

translations.literal: Xiang ordered subject to carry out killing—not subject's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang ordered me to strike—I am not to blame for his death.

sentences.zh: 苻登陛下末族，尚欲復讎，臣為兄報恥，于情理何負！

translations.literal: Fu Deng Your Majesty's marginal lineage—still desires revenge; subject for elder brother repays shame—in feeling and principle what fault!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng is only a distant clansman yet seeks vengeance for your murder—why should I be blamed for avenging my own brother?”

sentences.zh: 昔陛下假臣龍驤之號，謂臣曰：'朕以龍驤建業，卿其勉之！

translations.literal: Formerly Your Majesty lent subject Dragon-Soaring title, saying to subject: 'I by Dragon-Soaring founded enterprise—you must exert yourself!'
translations.idiomatic: Once you gave me the title Dragon-Soaring general and said, ‘I built my realm under that banner—see that you strive!’”

sentences.zh: '明詔昭然，言猶在耳。

translations.literal: 'Bright edict shining clear—words still in ears.
translations.idiomatic: Those words ring still in my ears.”

sentences.zh: 陛下雖過世為神，豈假手於苻登而圖臣，忘前征時言邪！

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty passed away and became spirit—could you lend hand through Fu Deng and plot against subject—forgetting former expedition-time words!
translations.idiomatic: Though you now dwell among the spirits, would you truly use Fu Deng as your weapon against me and forget what you swore on campaign?”

sentences.zh: 今為陛下立神象，可歸休於此，勿計臣過，聽臣至誠。

translations.literal: Now for Your Majesty erect spirit image—may return rest here; do not reckon subject's faults; hear subject's utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: I raise this effigy so your spirit may rest—ignore my faults and hear my heartfelt plea.”

sentences.zh: 」登進師攻萇，既而升樓謂萇曰：「自古及今，安有殺君而反立神象請福，望有益乎！

translations.literal: " Deng advanced army attacking Chang; afterward ascended tower speaking to Chang: "From antiquity to now—how can there be killing the lord yet erecting spirit image seeking blessing—hope there is benefit!
translations.idiomatic: ” Fu Deng pressed the assault, then mounted a tower and shouted at Yao Chang: “From antiquity to now, who ever murdered his sovereign and then raised an idol to beg fortune—do you expect reward?”

sentences.zh: 」大呼曰：「殺君賊姚萇出來，吾與汝決之，何為枉害無辜！

translations.literal: " Great called saying: "Lord-killing bandit Yao Chang come out—I with you decide it—why vainly harm guiltless!
translations.idiomatic: ” He roared, “Murderer Yao Chang, come out and fight me—why slaughter the innocent?”

sentences.zh: 」萇憚而不應。

translations.literal: " Chang feared and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yao Chang shrank back and gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 萇自立堅神象，戰未有利，軍中每夜驚恐，乃嚴鼓斬象首以送登。

translations.literal: Chang himself erected Jian spirit image; battle not yet favorable; army within each night alarmed and frightened—thereupon strict drums beheaded image head to send Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang had set up Fu Jian’s effigy, yet battle brought no luck and each night his camp panicked; he beat the drums, hacked off the statue’s head, and sent it to Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 登將軍竇洛、竇於等謀反發覺，出奔於萇。

translations.literal: Deng's generals Dou Luo, Dou Yu and others plotted rebellion discovered; fled out to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng’s generals Dou Luo and Dou Yu plotted revolt; exposed, they fled to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 登進討彭池不克，攻彌姐營及繁川諸堡，皆克之。

translations.literal: Deng advanced attacking Peng Pool without overcoming; attacked Mizijie camp and various forts of Fanchuan—all overcame them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng failed at Peng Pool but stormed Mizijie’s camp and the stockades along the Fanchuan, taking them all.

sentences.zh: 萇連戰屢敗，乃遣其中軍姚崇襲大界，登引師要之，大敗崇于安丘，俘斬二萬五千，進攻萇將吳忠、唐匡於平涼，克之，以尚書苻碩原為前禁將軍、滅羌校尉，戍平涼。

translations.literal: Chang repeatedly battled repeatedly defeated—thereupon dispatched his Central Army Yao Chong to raid Dajie; Deng led army to intercept him; greatly defeated Chong at Anqiu; captured and beheaded twenty-five thousand; advanced attacking Chang's generals Wu Zhong, Tang Kuang at Pingliang, overcame them; appointed Masters of Writing Fu Shuoyuan as Forward Prohibition General, Colonel Who Extinguishes the Qiang, garrison Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: After a string of defeats Yao Chang sent Yao Chong to strike Dajie; Fu Deng intercepted him at Anqiu, annihilated twenty-five thousand, then stormed Pingliang and captured Wu Zhong and Tang Kuang, naming Fu Shuoyuan forward prohibition general and colonel who exterminates the Qiang to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 登進據苟頭原以逼安定。

translations.literal: Deng advanced occupying Goutou Plain to press Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng seized Goutou Plain to threaten Anding.

sentences.zh: 萇率騎三萬夜襲大界營，陷之，殺登妻毛氏及其子弁、尚，擒名將數十人，驅掠男女五萬餘口而去。

translations.literal: Chang led thirty thousand cavalry night-raiding Dajie camp; overcame it; killed Deng's wife Lady Mao and his sons Bian and Shang; seized several tens of famous generals; drove and plundered men and women more than fifty thousand mouths and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang struck Dajie by night with thirty thousand horse, slew Fu Deng’s empress Lady Mao and princes Fu Bian and Fu Shang, bagged dozens of noted commanders, and marched away more than fifty thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 登收合餘兵，退據胡空堡，遣使齎書加竇沖大司馬、驃騎將軍、前鋒大都督、都督隴東諸軍事，楊定左丞相、上大將軍、都督中外諸軍事，楊璧大將軍、都督隴右諸軍事。
