translations.literal: Deng gathered remaining troops, retreated occupying Hu Kong fort; dispatched envoys bearing documents promoting Dou Chong Grand Marshal, General of Agile Cavalry, Forward Vanguard Grand Supervisor, Supervisor of Longdong Military Affairs; Yang Ding Left Chancellor, Supreme Grand General, Supervisor of All Military Affairs Within and Without; Yang Bi Grand General, Supervisor of Longyou Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng rallied his survivors at Hu Kong fort and sent orders naming Dou Chong grand marshal, grand general of agile cavalry, and supreme commander on the eastern Long corridor; Yang Ding left chancellor and supreme commander of all armies; Yang Bi grand general for the Longyou theater.

sentences.zh: 遣沖率見眾為先驅，自繁川趣長安。

translations.literal: He dispatched Chong leading present multitudes as vanguard; from Fanchuan hastened toward Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong was to lead the main body from Fanchuan toward Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 登率眾從新平逕據新豐之千戶固。

translations.literal: Deng led multitudes from Xinping directly occupying Xinfeng's Thousand-Household Stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng marched from Xinping straight to the Thousand-Household Redoubt at Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 使定率隴上諸軍為其後繼，璧留守仇池。

translations.literal: Ordered Ding to lead Longshang various armies as his rear succession; Bi stayed guarding Qiuachi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ding would bring up the Long ridge armies while Yang Bi stayed behind at Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 又命其并州刺史楊政、冀州刺史楊楷率所統大會長安。

translations.literal: Also ordered his Bing Inspector Yang Zheng, Ji Inspector Yang Kai to lead what they commanded great assembly at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He told Bingzhou governor Yang Zheng and Jizhou governor Yang Kai to converge on Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 萇遣其將軍王破虜略地秦州，楊定及破虜戰于清水之格奴阪，大敗之。

translations.literal: Chang dispatched his general Wang Polu raiding land Qinzhou; Yang Ding and Polu fought at Qingshui's Genu Slope; greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang sent Wang Polu to raid Qinzhou; Yang Ding met him at Genu Ford on the Qingshui and shattered his force.

sentences.zh: 登攻張龍世於鴦泉堡，姚萇救之，登引退。

translations.literal: Deng attacked Zhang Longshi at Mandarin-Duck Spring fort; Yao Chang rescued him; Deng led retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng besieged Zhang Longshi at Mandarin Spring fort until Yao Chang relieved him and Fu Deng withdrew.

sentences.zh: 萇密遣其將任瓫、宗度詐為內應，遣使招登，許開門納之。

translations.literal: Chang secretly dispatched his generals Ren Dun, Zong Du feigning as inner responders; dispatched envoys summoning Deng, promising opening gate admitting him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang secretly ordered Ren Dun and Zong Du to pose as defectors, inviting Fu Deng to enter an open gate.

sentences.zh: 登以為然。

translations.literal: Deng deemed it so.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng believed them.

sentences.zh: 雷惡地馳謂登曰：「姚萇多計略，善御人，必為奸變，願深宜詳思。

translations.literal: Le Erdi galloped saying to Deng: "Yao Chang has many stratagems, good at controlling people—surely will enact treacherous change—wish deeply should deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Le Erdi rode up warning Fu Deng, “Yao Chang is cunning and skilled at handling men—this must be a trap; think it through.”

sentences.zh: 」登乃止。

translations.literal: " Deng thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ” Fu Deng called off the advance.

sentences.zh: 萇聞惡地之詣登也，謂諸將曰：「此羌多奸智，今其詣登，事必無成。

translations.literal: Chang hearing Erdi's going to Deng, said to various generals: "This Qiang much treacherous wisdom—now his going to Deng—the affair surely will not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang heard Le Erdi had visited Fu Deng he told his officers, “That Qiang is full of guile; his counsel will spoil our plot.”

sentences.zh: 」登聞萇懸門以待之，大驚，謂左右曰：「雷征東其殆聖乎！

translations.literal: " Deng hearing Chang suspended gate awaiting him, greatly alarmed, said to left and right: "Le General Who Conquers the East—is he perhaps sagely!
translations.idiomatic: ” Learning Yao Chang had lifted the outer gates to lure him in, Fu Deng exclaimed to his staff, “General Le who conquers the east must be almost a sage!”

sentences.zh: 微此公，朕幾為豎子所誤。

translations.literal: Without this lord, I nearly was misled by petty fellows.
translations.idiomatic: Without him I would have fallen into that boy’s trap.”

sentences.zh: 」萇攻陷新羅堡。

translations.literal: " Chang attacked and overcame Xinluo fort.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yao Chang then took Xinluo fort.

sentences.zh: 萇撫風太守齊益男奔登。

translations.literal: Chang's Fufeng Administrator Qi Yinan fled to Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Yinan, Yao Chang’s prefect of Fufeng, defected to Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 登將軍路柴、強武等並以眾降於萇。

translations.literal: Deng's generals Lu Chai, Qiang Wu and others together with multitudes surrendered to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng’s generals Lu Chai and Qiang Wu brought their commands over to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 登攻萇將張業生於隴東，萇救之，不克而退。

translations.literal: Deng attacked Chang's general Zhang Yesheng east of Long; Chang rescued him; did not overcome and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng struck Zhang Yesheng in eastern Long; Yao Chang tried to relieve him but failed and drew back.

sentences.zh: 登將軍魏褐飛攻姚當成於杏城，為萇所殺。

translations.literal: Deng's general Wei Hefei attacked Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng; was killed by Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng’s general Wei Hefei attacked Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng and was slain by Yao Chang’s troops.

sentences.zh: 馮翊郭質起兵廣鄉以應登，宣檄三輔曰：「義感君子，利動小人。

translations.literal: Fengyi Guo Zhi raised troops at Guangxiang to respond to Deng; proclaimed to Three Assistants: "Righteousness moves gentlemen; profit stirs petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi of Fengyi rose at Guangxiang to support Fu Deng and circulated a manifesto through the Three Assistants: “Honor moves gentlemen; profit drives petty men.”

sentences.zh: 吾等生逢先帝堯、舜之化，累世受恩，非常伯納言之子，即卿校牧守之胤，而可坐視豺狼忍害君父！

translations.literal: We were born encountering Former Emperor Yao Shun transformation; accumulated generations received favor—if not Changbo Nayin's sons, then minister-colonel shepherd-guard heirs—how can sit watching wolves and jackals cruelly harm lord father!
translations.idiomatic: We grew up under our late sovereign’s humane rule; generations of our families served the throne—sons of high ministers or local governors—can we sit idle while jackals devour our ruler?”

sentences.zh: 裸屍薦棘，痛結幽泉，山陵無松隧之兆，靈主無清廟之頌，賊臣莫大之甚，自古所未聞。

translations.literal: Stripped corpse offered on thorns—pain knots hidden springs; hills and mounds lack pine-tunnel omens; spirit lord lacks clear-temple hymns—rebel minister none greater extreme—from antiquity never heard.
translations.idiomatic: His naked body was cast among brambles; no imperial tomb receives him, no hymn sounds in the ancestral shrine—such villainy is unheard of since history began.”

sentences.zh: 雖茹荼之苦，銜蓼之辛，何以諭之！

translations.literal: Although eating bitter-thistle bitterness, holding smartweed pungency—how with this instruct it!
translations.idiomatic: Wild rue and bitter herbs barely hint at our grief!”

sentences.zh: 姚萇窮凶肆害，毒被人神，於圖讖歷數萬無一分，而敢妄竊重名，厚顏瞬息，日月固所不照，二儀實亦不育。

translations.literal: Yao Chang utterly fierce spreads harm; poison spreads through men and spirits; in chart prophecy era fate ten thousand lacks one fraction—yet dares falsely steal heavy name; thick face in moment—sun and moon surely do not shine on him; two powers truly also do not nurture.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang piles crime upon crime; heaven grants him no shred of legitimacy in prophecy or mandate, yet he steals the imperial title—shameless for an instant; sun and moon refuse to shine on him and heaven and earth will not sustain him.”

sentences.zh: 皇天雖欲絕之，亦將假手於忠節。

translations.literal: August Heaven although desires to cut him off—also will lend hand through loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Though Heaven would blot him out, it will use loyal hearts as its weapon.”

sentences.zh: 凡百君子，皆夙漸神化，有懷義方，含恥而存，孰若蹈道而沒乎！

translations.literal: All hundred gentlemen—all early gradually divine transformation; harbor righteousness methods—bearing shame and surviving—how compared to treading the Way and perishing!
translations.idiomatic: Every gentleman among you has felt the court’s grace; will you nurse shame in silence or die walking the path of duty?”

sentences.zh: 」眾咸然之。

translations.literal: " The multitude all deemed it so.
translations.idiomatic: ” The crowd shouted assent.

sentences.zh: 唯鄭縣人苟曜不從，聚眾數千應姚萇。

translations.literal: Only Zheng county man Gou Yao did not follow; gathered multitudes several thousand responding to Yao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gou Yao of Zheng county refused, raising thousands for Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 登以質為平東將軍、馮翊太守。

translations.literal: Deng appointed Zhi as General Who Pacifies the East, Administrator of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng named Guo Zhi general who pacifies the east and Fengyi prefect.

sentences.zh: 質遣部將伐曜，大敗而歸。

translations.literal: Zhi dispatched subordinate generals attacking Yao; greatly defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi sent subordinates against Gou Yao and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 質乃東引楊楷，以為聲援，又與曜戰于鄭東，為曜所敗，遂歸於萇，萇以為將軍。

translations.literal: Zhi thereupon east drew Yang Kai, taking as sound aid; again with Yao fought east of Zheng; was defeated by Yao; thereupon returned to Chang; Chang appointed him general.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi called Yang Kai east for support, fought Gou Yao east of Zheng, lost, defected to Yao Chang, and was given a generalship.

sentences.zh: 質眾皆潰散。

translations.literal: Zhi's multitudes all scattered and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi’s army melted away.

sentences.zh: 登自雍攻萇將金溫于范氏堡，克之，遂渡渭水，攻萇京兆太守韋范于段氏堡，不克，進據曲牢。

translations.literal: Deng from Yong attacked Chang's general Jin Wen at Fan clan fort, overcame it; thereupon crossed Wei River; attacked Chang's Jingzhao Administrator Wei Fan at Duan clan fort; did not overcome; advanced occupying Qulao.
translations.idiomatic: From Yong Fu Deng stormed Jin Wen at Fan’s fort, crossed the Wei, failed against Jingzhao prefect Wei Fan at Duan’s fort, but seized Qulao.

sentences.zh: 苟曜有眾一萬，據逆方堡，密應登，登去曲牢繁川，次於馬頭願。

translations.literal: Gou Yao had multitudes ten thousand; occupied Nifang fort; secretly responded to Deng; Deng left Qulao Fanchuan; halted at Matouyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Yao held ten thousand men at Nifang fort in secret league with Fu Deng; Fu Deng moved from Qulao through Fanchuan and camped at Matouyuan.

sentences.zh: 萇率騎來距，大戰敗之，斬其尚書吳忠，進攻新平。

translations.literal: Chang led cavalry coming to resist; great battle defeated him; beheaded his Masters of Writing Wu Zhong; advanced attacking Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang rode out to oppose him, shattered Fu Deng’s army, slew minister Wu Zhong, and pressed toward Xinping.

sentences.zh: 萇率眾救之，登引退，復攻安定，為萇所敗，據路承堡。

translations.literal: Chang led multitudes rescuing them; Deng led retreat; again attacked Anding; was defeated by Chang; occupied Lucheng fort.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang relieved Xinping; Fu Deng withdrew, struck Anding, lost, and fell back to Lucheng fort.

sentences.zh: 是時萇疾病，見苻堅為崇。

translations.literal: At this time Chang was ill; saw Fu Jian as haunting.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yao Chang lay sick, haunted by visions of Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 登聞之，秣馬萬兵，告堅神主曰：「曾孫登自受任執戈，幾將一紀，未嘗不上天錫祐，皇鑒垂矜，所在必克，賊旅冰摧。

translations.literal: Deng hearing it, foddered horses ten thousand troops; announced to Jian spirit lord: "Great-grandson Deng from receiving commission grasping spear—nearly will one cycle—not once did not ascend Heaven grant blessing, August Mirror suspend pity—wherever located surely overcame—bandit hosts ice shattered.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng fed his horses and massed the army, telling Fu Jian’s tablet, “Your great-grandson has borne spear and shield almost twelve years; heaven has favored every battle and shattered Yao’s ranks like ice.”

sentences.zh: 今太皇帝之靈降災疢於逆羌，以形類推之，醜虜必將不振。

translations.literal: Now Grand Emperor's spirit sends sickness on rebellious Qiang—by form category extrapolating—ugly captives surely will not revive.
translations.idiomatic: Now your spirit sends plague upon the rebel Qiang—surely they must soon collapse.”

sentences.zh: 登當因其隕斃，順行天誅，拯復梓宮，謝罪清廟。

translations.literal: Deng ought follow their fall death; comply executing Heaven's punishment; rescue restore catalpa palace; apologize guilt at Clear Temple.
translations.idiomatic: I will seize their dying breath to execute heaven’s sentence, recover your coffin, and offer apology in the bright shrine.”

sentences.zh: 」於是大赦境內，百僚進位二等。

translations.literal: " Thereupon greatly pardoned within territory; hundred officials advanced rank two grades.
translations.idiomatic: ” He declared a general amnesty and promoted every official two ranks.

sentences.zh: 與萇將姚崇爭麥于清水，累為崇所敗。

translations.literal: With Chang's general Yao Chong contested wheat at Qingshui; repeatedly was defeated by Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He sparred with Yao Chong over the wheat fields along the Qingshui and suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 進逼安定，去城九十餘里。

translations.literal: Advanced pressing Anding; removed from city more than ninety li.
translations.idiomatic: He closed to within ninety li of Anding.

sentences.zh: 萇疾小瘳，率眾距登，登去營逆萇，萇遣其將姚熙隆別攻登營，登懼，退還。

translations.literal: Chang's illness small recovered; led multitudes resisting Deng; Deng left camp opposing Chang; Chang dispatched his general Yao Xilong separately attacking Deng camp; Deng feared; retreated returning.
translations.idiomatic: As Yao Chang rallied he blocked Fu Deng; Fu Deng left camp to meet him, but Yao Xilong struck Fu Deng’s rear and forced him to flee.

sentences.zh: 萇夜引軍過登營三十餘里以躡登後。

translations.literal: Chang night led army passing Deng camp more than thirty li to tread Deng's rear.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yao Chang slipped past Fu Deng’s camp and seized his rear line thirty li away.

sentences.zh: 旦而候人告曰：「賊諸營已空，不知所向。

translations.literal: Dawn and scout reported saying: "Bandit various camps already empty—do not know where headed.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn scouts reported, “The enemy camps stand empty—none know where they went.”

sentences.zh: 」登驚曰：「此為何人，去令我不知，來令我不覺，謂其將死，忽然復來，朕與此羌同世，何其厄哉！

translations.literal: " Deng alarmed said: "This is what kind of person—going makes me not know; coming makes me not perceive—said he about to die; suddenly again comes—I with this Qiang same generation—how bitter!
translations.idiomatic: ” Fu Deng cried, “What manner of foe slips away unseen and strikes unwarned? I thought him dying, yet he returns—I share an age with this Qiang and fate is cruel!”

sentences.zh: 」遂罷師還雍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon dismissed army returning Yong.
translations.idiomatic: ” He broke off the campaign and withdrew to Yong.

sentences.zh: 以竇沖為右丞相。

translations.literal: Appointed Dou Chong Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong became right chancellor.

sentences.zh: 尋而沖叛，自稱秦王，建年號。

translations.literal: Soon Chong rebelled; self-titled King of Qin; established era name.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dou Chong rebelled, styled himself king of Qin, and minted an era name.

sentences.zh: 登攻之於野人堡，沖請救于姚萇，萇遣其太子興攻胡空堡以救之。

translations.literal: Deng attacked him at Wild Man fort; Chong requested rescue from Yao Chang; Chang dispatched his heir apparent Xing attacking Hu Kong fort to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng besieged him at Wild Man fort; Dou Chong begged Yao Chang for aid, and Yao Chang sent crown prince Yao Xing against Hu Kong fort to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 登引兵還赴胡空堡，沖遂與萇連和。

translations.literal: Deng led troops returning hastening to Hu Kong fort; Chong thereupon with Chang linked peace.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng raced back to Hu Kong fort, whereupon Dou Chong allied with Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 至是萇死，登聞之喜曰：「姚興小兒，吾將折杖以笞之。

translations.literal: By this Chang died; Deng hearing it joyfully said: "Yao Xing petty boy—I will break rod to whip him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang died Fu Deng crowed, “Yao Xing is a mere boy—I will thrash him with a stick.”

sentences.zh: 」於是大赦，盡眾而東，攻屠各姚奴、帛蒲二堡，克之，自甘泉向關中。

translations.literal: " Thereupon greatly pardoned; exhausted multitudes east; attacked Tuge Yao Nu, Bo Pu two forts; overcame them; from Ganquan toward Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: ” He declared amnesty, threw every man eastward, stormed the Tuge forts of Yao Nu and Bo Pu, and marched from Ganquan toward Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 興追登不及數十里，登從六陌趣廢橋，興將尹緯據橋以待之。

translations.literal: Xing pursued Deng not reaching several tens of li; Deng from Liumo hastened toward Defunct Bridge; Xing's general Yin Wei occupied bridge awaiting him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing pursued within a few dozen li; Fu Deng raced by Liumo toward the ruined bridge where Yin Wei waited.

sentences.zh: 登爭水不得，眾渴死者十二三。

translations.literal: Deng contested water could not obtain; multitude thirst-dead twelve or thirteen in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Denied the river, his men died of thirst by the thousands.

sentences.zh: 與緯大戰，為緯所敗，其夜眾潰，登單馬奔雍。

translations.literal: With Wei great battle; was defeated by Wei; that night multitudes scattered; Deng single horse fled to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Yin Wei and lost; that night his army collapsed and Fu Deng galloped alone to Yong.

sentences.zh: 初，登之東也，留其弟司徒廣守雍，太子崇守胡空堡。

translations.literal: Initially, when Deng's easting, left his younger brother Minister of Education Guang guarding Yong; heir apparent Chong guarding Hu Kong fort.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Deng marched east he had left his brother Fu Guang as minister of education at Yong and crown prince Fu Chong at Hu Kong fort.

sentences.zh: 廣、崇聞登敗，出奔，眾散。

translations.literal: Guang, Chong hearing Deng defeated; fled out; multitudes scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Guang and Fu Chong heard of the defeat they fled and their troops scattered.

sentences.zh: 登至，無所歸，遂奔平涼，收集遺眾入馬毛山。

translations.literal: Deng arrived; nowhere to return; thereupon fled Pingliang; gathered remnant multitudes entering Maomao Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng found no haven at Yong, fled to Pingliang, and rallied survivors on Maomao Mountain.

sentences.zh: 興率眾攻之，登遣子汝陰王宗質於隴西鮮卑乞伏乾歸，結婚請援，乾歸遣騎二萬救登。

translations.literal: Xing led multitudes attacking him; Deng dispatched son Prince of Ru'yin Zong as hostage to Longxi Xianbei Qifu Qiangui; allied marriage requesting aid; Qiangui dispatched twenty thousand cavalry rescuing Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing pressed the mountain; Fu Deng sent his son Prince of Ru’yin Fu Zong as hostage to the Longxi Xianbei Qifu Qiangui, sealed the pact by marriage, and Qifu Qiangui rode to his aid with twenty thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 登引軍出迎，與興戰于山南，為興所敗，登被殺。

translations.literal: Deng led army out welcoming; with Xing fought south of mountain; was defeated by Xing; Deng was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng came down to meet them, fought Yao Xing south of the mountain, lost, and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 在位九年，時年五十二。

translations.literal: On throne nine years; at time age fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He had reigned nine years and was fifty-two when he fell.

sentences.zh: 崇奔於湟中，僭稱尊號，改元延初。

translations.literal: Chong fled to Huangzhong; arrogated exalted title; changed era to Yanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chong fled to the Huang River basin, claimed the throne, and adopted the era name Yanxi.

sentences.zh: 偽諡登曰高皇帝，廟號太宗。

translations.literal: Falsely posthumously titled Deng as Emperor Gao; temple name Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: They honored Fu Deng posthumously as Emperor Gao with temple name Taizong.

sentences.zh: 崇為乾歸所逐，崇、定皆死。

translations.literal: Chong was driven by Qiangui; Chong, Ding all died.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Qiangui drove out Fu Chong; both Fu Chong and Yang Ding perished.

sentences.zh: 始，健以穆帝永和七年僭立，至登五世，凡四十有四歲，以孝武帝太元十九年滅。

translations.literal: Beginning, Jian in Emperor Mu's Yonghe seventh year arrogated establishment; reaching Deng five generations; altogether forty-four years; in Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan nineteenth year extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jiàn had seized the throne in Yonghe seven (351) under Emperor Mu; five rulers later, after forty-four years, the house fell in Taiyuan nineteen (394) under Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 索泮，字德林，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Suo Pan, courtesy name Delin, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Pan, courtesy name Delin, came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 世為冠族。

translations.literal: For generations they were cap-and-girdle lineage.
translations.idiomatic: His clan ranked among the great houses for generations.

sentences.zh: 泮少時遊俠，及長，變節好學，有佐世才器。

translations.literal: Pan in youth roamed knight-errant; reaching maturity, changed measure loving learning; had assisting-age talent vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Suo Pan lived by the sword; grown, he reformed, turned scholar, and showed gifts fit for governing the age.

sentences.zh: 張天錫輔政，以泮為冠軍、記室參軍。

translations.literal: Zhang Tianxi assisted governance; appointed Pan Champion and Recorder Staff Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhang Tianxi directed the government he named Suo Pan champion general and secretary-adjunct.

sentences.zh: 天錫即位，拜司兵，歷位禁中錄事。

translations.literal: Tianxi ascended throne; appointed Minister of War; passed through posts as Palace Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Tianxi took the throne Suo Pan became director of military affairs and rose through palace recorder posts.

sentences.zh: 執法禦掾，州府肅然，郡縣改跡。

translations.literal: Upholding law controlling clerk—prefecture office solemn; commanderies and counties changed tracks.
translations.idiomatic: As judicial inspector he struck awe through the provincial seat and transformed conduct in every county.

sentences.zh: 遷羽林左監，有勤幹之稱。

translations.literal: Promoted Feathered Forest Left Commandant; had diligent capability reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to commandant of the left feathered forest, he earned renown for tireless efficiency.

sentences.zh: 出為中壘將軍、西郡武威太守、典戎校尉。

translations.literal: Exited as Central Rampart General, Western Commandery Wuwei Administrator, Colonel in Charge of Troops.
translations.idiomatic: He left court as central rampart general, prefect of Wuwei in the western commandery, and colonel of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 政務寬和，戎夏懷其惠，天錫甚敬之。

translations.literal: Government affairs lenient and harmonious; barbarians and Xia cherished his kindness; Tianxi greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was mild and fair; tribesmen and Chinese alike cherished his kindness, and Zhang Tianxi held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 苻堅見而歎曰：「涼州信多君子！

translations.literal: Fu Jian seeing sighed saying: "Liangzhou truly many gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian exclaimed on meeting him, “Liangzhou breeds true gentlemen!”

sentences.zh: 」既而以泮河西德望，拜別駕。

translations.literal: " Afterward because Pan had Hexi virtue renown; appointed Attendant Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: ” Soon Suo Pan’s reputation west of the Yellow River won him appointment as provincial attendant clerk.

sentences.zh: 呂光既克姑臧，泮固郡不降，光攻而獲之。

translations.literal: Lü Guang having overcome Guzang; Pan firmly held commandery not surrendering; Guang attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Guang took Guzang Suo Pan barred his prefecture until Lü Guang stormed it and seized him.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「孤既平西域，將赴難京師，梁熙無狀，絕孤歸路，此朝延之罪人，卿何意阻郡固迷，自同元惡！

translations.literal: Guang said: "I having pacified Western Regions, about to go to capital crisis—Liang Xi without manner cut off my return road—this court-extending's crime person—what intention do you block commandery stubbornly deluded, equating yourself with chief villain!
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang said, “I conquered the west and marched to rescue the capital; Liang Xi blocked my road—he is the dynasty’s criminal—why do you cling to your county like the arch-villain?”

sentences.zh: 」泮厲色責光曰：「將軍受詔討叛胡，可受詔亂涼州邪？

translations.literal: " Pan stern-faced reproached Guang saying: "General received edict attacking rebellious Hu—can receive edict disturbing Liangzhou!
translations.idiomatic: ” Suo Pan answered sternly, “You were ordered to punish rebel tribes—were you ordered to ravage Liangzhou?”

sentences.zh: 寡君何罪，而將軍害之？

translations.literal: Our lord what crime—yet General harmed him?
translations.idiomatic: What crime had our sovereign committed that you destroyed him?”

sentences.zh: 泮但苦力寡，不能固守以報君父之讎，豈如逆氐彭濟望風反叛！

translations.literal: Pan only bitter strength few—could not firmly guard to repay lord-father's vengeance—how like rebellious Di Peng Ji watching wind rebelling!
translations.idiomatic: I regret only my weakness—I could not hold the walls to avenge my ruler; do you compare me to Peng Ji the traitorous Di who switched sides at the rumor of war?”

sentences.zh: 主滅臣死，禮之常也。

translations.literal: Lord extinguished subject dies—rite's constant.
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign falls his minister follows—that is the constant teaching of ritual.”

sentences.zh: 」乃就刑於市，神色不變。

translations.literal: " Thereupon faced execution at market; expression unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: ” He went to execution in the marketplace without changing color.

sentences.zh: 弟菱，有俊才，仕張天錫為執法中郎、冗從右監。

translations.literal: Younger brother Ling had outstanding talent; served Zhang Tianxi as Law-Enforcing Gentleman and Supernumerary Right Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Suo Ling, a brilliant man, served Zhang Tianxi as law-enforcing gentleman and supernumerary attendant of the right.

sentences.zh: 苻堅世至伏波將軍、典農都尉，與泮俱被害。

translations.literal: In Jian's age reached General Who Calms the Waves, Colonel Director of Agriculture—with Pan together was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Jian he rose to general who calms the waves and colonel director of agriculture, and died with Suo Pan.

sentences.zh: 徐嵩，字元高，盛之子也。

translations.literal: Xu Song, courtesy name Yuangao, was Sheng's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Song, courtesy name Yuangao, was the son of Xu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 少以清白著稱。

translations.literal: From youth by purity was famed.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known for honest administration.

sentences.zh: 苻堅時舉賢良，為郎中，稍遷長安令，貴戚子弟犯法者，嵩一皆考竟，請托路絕。

translations.literal: In Fu Jian's time recommended Worthy and Good; became Gentleman; gradually promoted Chang'an Magistrate—noble in-law sons who violated law—Song all examined to end—request-recommendation road cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as worthy under Fu Jian, he served as gentleman of the palace, then magistrate of Chang’an, brought every lawbreaking noble scion to justice, and shut the door to influence peddling.

sentences.zh: 堅甚奇之，謂其叔父成曰：「人為長吏，故當應耳。

translations.literal: Jian greatly deemed him extraordinary; said to his uncle Cheng: "Others being senior clerks—thus ought merely comply.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian marveled and told Xu Song’s uncle Cheng, “Most men fill high office by mere competence.”

sentences.zh: 此年少落落，有端貳之才。

translations.literal: This youth broad and outstanding—has heir-assistant talent.
translations.idiomatic: This young man stands apart—he has the makings of a chief minister.”

sentences.zh: 」遷守始平郡，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: " Promoted guarding Shiping commandery—very had awe and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xu Song was promoted to Shiping commandery, where terror and kindness mingled in his rule.

sentences.zh: 及壘陷，姚方成執而數之，嵩厲色謂方成曰：「汝姚萇罪應萬死，主上止黃眉之斬而宥之，叨據內外，位為列將，無犬馬識養之誠，首為大逆。

translations.literal: When rampart fell, Yao Fangcheng seized and reproached him; Song stern-faced said to Fangcheng: "Your Yao Chang crime deserves ten thousand deaths—Sovereign stopped Huangmei's beheading and pardoned him—shamelessly occupied inside and outside—position as ranked general—without dog-horse knowing-nurture sincerity—first enacted great rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When the fort fell Yao Fangcheng seized him for rebuke; Xu Song snarled, “Yao Chang deserved death ten thousand times over; our sovereign spared him when Deng Qi wanted his head, yet he clawed his way to power as a general without the loyalty of a dog or horse and became arch-traitor.”

sentences.zh: 汝曹羌輩豈可以人理期也！

translations.literal: You bunch Qiang crowd—how can by human principle be expected!
translations.idiomatic: How can one reason with you Qiang like men?”

sentences.zh: 何不速殺我，早見先帝，取姚萇於地下。

translations.literal: Why not quickly kill me—early see Former Emperor—seize Yao Chang under ground.
translations.idiomatic: Kill me now so I may greet the late emperor and drag Yao Chang down to hell.”

sentences.zh: 」方成怒，三斬嵩，漆其首為便器。

translations.literal: " Fangcheng angry—three cut Song—lacquered his head as toilet vessel.
translations.idiomatic: ” Enraged, Fangcheng hacked Xu Song to pieces and lacquered his skull into a chamber pot.

sentences.zh: 登哭之哀慟，贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: Deng wept for him mournfully greatly; gifted General of Chariots and Cavalry, ceremonies equal Three Offices; posthumous title Loyal Martial.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng mourned him bitterly, posthumously naming him grand general of chariots and cavalry with three-duke honors and the epithet Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自兩京殄覆，九土分崩，赤縣成蛇豕之墟，紫宸遷蛙黽之穴，干戈日用，戰爭方興，猶逐鹿之並驅，若瞻烏之靡定。

translations.literal: Historian says: From two capitals extinct-overturned, nine soils split-collapse—Red County became snake-boar ruins—Purple Palace moved frog-toad burrows—shields and spears daily used—warfare just rising—like chasing deer together galloping—like gazing crows nowhere settled.
translations.idiomatic: The historians say: After the twin capitals fell and the realm shattered, the Chinese heartland became a lair of serpents and swine and the throne a frog’s burrow; arms clashed daily like hunters chasing the deer and crows seeking an uncertain perch.

sentences.zh: 苻洪擅蠻陬之桀黠，乘羯虜之危亡，乃附款江東而志圖關右，禍生蠆毒，未逞狼心。

translations.literal: Fu Hong monopolized barbarian corner's fierce cunning—rode Jie captives' peril death—then attached allegiance Jiangdong while ambition plotted Guan right—calamity born scorpion poison—not yet realize wolf heart.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hong seized his frontier with savage cunning, exploited the Jie collapse, courted the eastern court while eyeing the northwest; poison gathered before his wolfish ambition could run free.

sentences.zh: 健既承家，克隆凶緒，率思歸之眾，投山西之隙，據億丈之岩險，總三秦之果銳，敢窺大寶，遂竊鴻名，校數奸雄，有可言矣。

translations.literal: Jian having inherited house—able enlarged fierce thread—led homesick multitudes—threw Shaanxi's crack—occupied billion-fathom cliff peril—gathered three Qin's fruit sharp—dared peer great treasure—thereupon stole grand name—compare count treacherous heroes—has what can be said.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jiàn inherited that legacy, led homesick hosts through the Shanxi gap, seized its towering passes and Qin’s fiercest blades, dared covet the great treasure and steal a majestic title—among pretenders he merits comparison.

sentences.zh: 長生慘虐，稟自率由。

translations.literal: Changsheng cruel slaughter—inherited from following self.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng’s cruelty flowed from wanton caprice.

sentences.zh: 睹辰象之災，謂法星之夜飲；

translations.literal: Seeing celestial phenomena's calamity—called Law Star's night drinking;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing omens in the stars, he imagined the law planet drunk by night;

sentences.zh: 忍生靈之命，疑猛獸之朝饑。

translations.literal: Endured living kind's lives—suspected fierce beasts' morning hunger.
translations.idiomatic: he toyed with lives as if guessing when hungry beasts would next feed.

sentences.zh: 但肆毒于刑殘，曾無心於戒懼。

translations.literal: Only spread poison in punishment mutilation—never had heart in guard fear.
translations.idiomatic: He poured poison into torture and never thought of restraint.

sentences.zh: 招亂速禍，不亦宜乎！

translations.literal: Summon chaos hasten calamity—is it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder his recklessness hastened disaster!”

sentences.zh: 永固雅量瑰姿，變夷眾夏，葉魚龍之謠詠，挺草付之休征，克翦奸回，纂承偽曆，遵明王之德教，闡先聖之儒風，撫育黎元，憂勤庶政。

translations.literal: Yonggu elegant measure rare bearing—transformed barbarians gathered Xia—matched fish-dragon ballad chant—upheld grass-fu auspicious omen—able cut treacherous deviant—inherited false calendar—followed enlightened king's virtue teaching—expounded former sage's Confucian wind—nurtured black-haired people—worried diligent myriad governance.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian, styled Yonggu, bore majestic bearing; he turned tribes into subjects and fulfilled the fish-dragon prophecies and the “grass fu” omens, cut down villains, seized the illicit throne, honored royal virtue, spread Confucian teaching, nurtured the people, and toiled at every duty.

sentences.zh: 王猛以宏材緯軍國，苻融以懿戚贊經綸，權薛以諒直進規謨，鄧、張以忠勇恢威略，俊賢效足，杞梓呈才，文武兼施，德刑具舉。

translations.literal: Wang Meng by grand talent weaved army state—Fu Rong by imperial kin assisted warp-weft—Quan Xue by honest straight advanced regulations—Deng, Zhang by loyal brave expanded might strategy—handsome worthies offered feet—qi zi trees presented talent—civil martial both applied—virtue punishment both raised.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng ordered state and army with vast talent; Fu Rong, imperial kin, guided policy; Quan and Xue offered blunt counsel; Deng and Zhang expanded power with loyalty and valor—worthy men thronged his court like prized timber, civil and military arms worked together, virtue and punishment both found their place.

sentences.zh: 乃平燕定蜀，擒代吞涼，跨三分之二，居九州之七，遐荒慕義，幽險宅心，因止馬而獻歌，托棲鸞以成頌，因以功侔曩烈，豈直化洽當年！

translations.literal: Thereupon pacified Yan settled Shu—captured Dai swallowed Liang—spanned two-thirds three—dwelt nine provinces' seven—distant waste admired righteousness—hidden peril lodged hearts—because stopping horse presented songs—entrusted perching luan to complete hymns—thereby merit matched former bursts—how merely transform harmonize present year!
translations.idiomatic: He crushed Yan, subdued Shu, seized Dai, annexed Liang, held two-thirds of the realm and seven of nine provinces; frontier peoples pledged loyalty, remote fastnesses bowed their hearts; poets halted his horse with songs and praised phoenix roosts—his feats rival antiquity’s heroes, far more than momentary peace.

sentences.zh: 雖五胡之盛，莫之比也。

translations.literal: Although Five Hu's flourishing—none compared to him.
translations.idiomatic: Even at the height of the Five Hu none matched him.

sentences.zh: 既而足己誇世，愎諫違謀，輕敵怒鄰，窮兵黷武。

translations.literal: Thenafter self-satisfied boasting age—stubborn remonstrance oppose plans—despise enemy anger neighbors—exhaust troops abuse weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Then he grew complacent, spurned advice, slighted foes and provoked neighbors, and exhausted the realm in wars.

sentences.zh: 懟三正之未葉，恥五運之猶乖，傾率土之師，起滔天之寇，負其犬羊之力，肆其吞噬之能。

translations.literal: Resent three rectifiers' not harmonized—shame five revolutions' still awry—tilt entire earth's hosts—raise overflowing-heaven's bandits—bear their dog-sheep strength—unleash their swallow-devour capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Resenting heaven’s seasons and ashamed the dynastic cycle still misfit, he hurled the whole army into rebel tides, trusting barbarian strength and devouring ambition.

sentences.zh: 自謂戰必勝，攻必取，便欲鳴鸞禹穴，駐蹕疑山，疏爵以侯楚材，築館以須歸命。

translations.literal: Self-called battle surely wins—attack surely takes—then wished cry luan at Yu's cave—halt imperial halt at Yi Mountain—scatter noble ranks to await Chu timber—build lodges to await surrender mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Certain every battle would bring victory, he dreamed of halting his chariot at Yu’s shrine on Mount Yi, ennobling Jin subjects and building lodges for surrendered emperors.

sentences.zh: 曾弗知人道助順，神理害盈，雖矜涿野之強，終致昆陽之敗。

translations.literal: Never knew human way aids obedience—divine pattern harms fullness—although boasting Zhuoye's strength—ultimately brought Kunyang's defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored that heaven favors the just and punishes pride; though he boasted like King Wu at Zhuolu, he ended like Wang Mang at Kunyang.

sentences.zh: 遂使凶渠候隙，狡寇伺間，步搖啟其禍先，燒當乘其亂極，宗社遷於他族，身首罄於賊臣，貽戒將來，取笑天下，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Thereby caused fierce leaders await crack—cunning bandits spy gap—Buyao opened their calamity first—Shaodang rode their chaos extreme—ancestral altars moved to other clan—body head exhausted at rebel ministers—leave warning future—invite laugh world—is it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Thus jackals watched for openings: Murong struck first, Shaodang Qiang rode the turmoil, the altars passed to strangers, his body fell to traitors—a warning and a jest to the world—how pitiful!

sentences.zh: 豈不謬哉！

translations.literal: Is it not erroneous!
translations.idiomatic: What folly!

sentences.zh: 苻丕承亂僭竊，尋及傾敗，斯可謂天之所廢，人不能支。

translations.literal: Fu Pi inherited chaos usurp-stole—soon reached overturn defeat—this can be called Heaven's what abolishes—men cannot support.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi seized power amid ruin and quickly collapsed—truly heaven withdrew its mandate and no man could save him.

sentences.zh: 苻登集離散之兵，厲死休之志，雖眾寡不敵，難以立功，而義烈慷慨，有足稱矣。

translations.literal: Fu Deng gathered scattered troops—sharpened death-rest intent—although multitude few not matched—hard to establish merit—yet righteousness fierce generous—has worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng rallied broken armies with banners sworn to fight to the death; though outnumbered and unable to restore the realm, his fervor deserved praise.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：洪惟壯勇，威棱氐種。

translations.literal: Praise says: Hong only stalwart brave—awe edge Di race.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Fu Hong towered in courage and struck awe among the Di.

sentences.zh: 健藉世資，遂雄關、隴。

translations.literal: Jian relied generation capital—thereupon heroic Guan, Long.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jiàn rode his inheritance to mastery of the passes and Longxi.

sentences.zh: 長生昏虐，敗不旋踵。

translations.literal: Changsheng dark cruel—defeat not turn heel.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng’s blind cruelty brought ruin before he could turn round.

sentences.zh: 永固禎祥，肇自龍驤。

translations.literal: Yonggu auspicious omens—began from Dragon-Soaring.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian’s fortune rose from the Dragon-Soaring command.

sentences.zh: 垂旒負扆，竊帝圖王。

translations.literal: Hanging tassels bearing yi screen—stole emperor plotted king.
translations.idiomatic: Veiled king though he was, he stole the mantle of emperor.

sentences.zh: 患生縱敵，難起矜強。

translations.literal: Calamity born indulging enemy—hardship arose boasting strength.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster came from sparing foes and pride in naked force.

sentences.zh: 丕、登僭假，淪胥以亡。

translations.literal: Pi, Deng usurp false—sink together thereby perish.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi and Fu Deng ruled as pretenders and sank together into oblivion.
